- Absolute timings are not used as tests, because they are too unreliable on shared machines; the targets of section 10 are design targets, secured by the size budget and the complexity checks

Feedback, reports and signals:

- Private feedback inbox (optional): instead of a GitHub issue, feedback can be sent to the server's inbox, end-to-end encrypted on the device with the operator's public key; the server stores only ciphertext, the operator collects and decrypts it on their own device, and it is deleted from the server after collection; available to accounts with the permission flag, assigned at first as an experiment to a share of accounts (an account is a tree, so the app offers the inbox if any tree on the device has the permission); the operator's public key is reported by the server with the capabilities; an operations flag can switch the inbox off; only on the user's initiative, with the same preview; the IP address is not stored; what arrives is untrusted input, and the operator decides what becomes a GitHub issue
- Diagnostics view: the app shows its timing marks and the shape of the tree on demand, only on the device
- Performance report: if a user finds the app too slow, they can send a report containing only numbers: timings, app version, build and environment, storage engine, AOT or interpreted, browser and operating system family, screen size class, the active switches (release, experiment and permission flags, the tree features of the affected tree, whether experimental features are on for this device), and the shape of the tree (number of items and events, depth, maximum width, distribution of note lengths, number of relations and conflicts); never titles, notes, names, device labels, display names, ids or timestamps; the user sees the report before sending and can edit or cancel it
- The report is sent as a pre-filled GitHub issue that the user submits themselves, or copied or saved as a file, or optionally sent to the private feedback inbox end-to-end encrypted to the operator ([ADR-055](item:faf555b0-b43a-58c1-bdd7-c1e0a73c91a3)); never unencrypted through a server; the app says that a GitHub issue is linked to the user's GitHub account and public
- Reports are untrusted input: the report is a JSON block with a fixed schema; the pipeline reads only that block, validated against the schema, and ignores all free text; agents treat it as data, never as instructions; a human label decides whether a report is worked on
- From the tree shape in a report the harness generates a synthetic dataset of the same shape to reproduce the slowdown; once the cause is found, the dataset joins the reference datasets and its complexity check becomes a gate
- Signals for bets (ADRs of kind `bet`) through the feedback form: each bet can define a few optional signal questions with fixed answer choices, shown in the feedback form; users can also tick "include usage summary": counts and shares computed on the device from one tree the user chooses (for example sync mode in use, conflicts resolved in the last 30 days, uses of predefined versus own relation types without names, share of titles with Markdown, median taps to capture); never content, names or timestamps; never automatic or by default; shared trees are excluded, because they contain other people's activity (only the number of trees and of shared trees on the device may be counted); shown in the preview like everything else
- Local usage counters: the counts needed for usage summaries are kept on the device only, per tree, as daily totals for at most 30 days; never synced, never sent except in a usage summary the user ticks
- Every signal is defined in its bet card with exactly the numbers it collects; a new signal needs human approval
- A regular agent review (for example monthly, as an issue) counts signal answers per bet and, when a review trigger has occurred, proposes a review of the ADR with the numbers; the decision stays with the owner
- The report format is designed so that error reports (what went wrong and where in the code, without content) can use it later

Manual tests and feedback:

- The owner's daily use on phone, tablet and desktop is the main manual test
- In-app feedback: users (and the owner) send findings (bug, usability, accessibility, performance, other) from within the app, using the same mechanism as the performance report: a pre-filled GitHub issue the user submits, copy or file, or the private feedback inbox ([ADR-055](item:faf555b0-b43a-58c1-bdd7-c1e0a73c91a3)); the user's own description, plus optionally the diagnostics block with numbers only; previewed and editable; never unencrypted through a server; free text is untrusted input ([ADR-051](item:70d87940-8c95-593a-ba9d-aa3fd8631e22)); a human label decides whether agents work on it; the feedback form itself is accessible
- Release check: before promotion to production, the owner runs a guided check of about five minutes on each device (release 1: phone, tablet and desktop; later releases: the phone and every device type whose code changed), shown in the test build of the app: the update arrives and is applied with consent; the tree is complete; sync works; on the iPhone started from the home screen and offline (on a borrowed iPhone, see the Safari decision); the result is sent with the same mechanism as an issue linked to the release, and is part of the manual approval
- Exploratory testing by an agent: nightly or before a release, an agent uses the app with tasks (for example "collect ideas for a trip and sort them", "share a tree") at phone size and with keyboard only, and reports what was confusing, slow or broken; findings become issues that need a human label
- No paid device clouds; free programmes for open-source projects can be checked once the repository is public

Compiler and analyzers (the first gate):

- Nullable reference types on, warnings treated as errors, .NET analyzers at a strict level, `dotnet format` checked in CI
- Banned API analyzer (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BannedApiAnalyzers): forbidden calls (for example `DateTime.Now`, `Guid.NewGuid`, `new Random`, browser and I/O APIs in Domain) are compile errors with a message saying why
- Snapshot files of Verify (`*.verified.*`) are protected like the stored test data: CI never accepts new snapshots automatically, and changes need human approval

Principles that shape the code from the start:

- Everything random or time-based is replaceable: time comes only through .NET's `TimeProvider`, ids and random values (item ids, event ids, nonces, the random sync moment) through a replaceable generator, so every test can be reproduced exactly
- Several devices can be simulated in one process without a browser: the local store sits behind an interface with an in-memory implementation, and transports, scheduler and clock are replaceable; simulations run many devices with random online and offline phases, clock offsets, duplicate imports and merges, and check that all end with the same tree and the same conflicts
- Stored formats are tested for compatibility: a collection of real stored data (events, envelopes, export files, pairing codes) from every released version is kept in the repository and read by every new version; the previously released Domain version reads events of the new version and must still see every item and every text (rules 1 to 4 of event versioning); fixed test data for encryption makes sure a library update cannot silently change the format

Testing rules:

- The Domain project carries most of the logic and is covered by unit tests without browser or server
- Property-based tests check convergence: the same set of events, in any arrival order and with duplicates, always gives the same tree; further ones cover cycles, references to deleted or moved siblings, conflicts and replay after snapshots
- Privacy is tested automatically: padding sizes, no IP addresses or receive times stored, neutral `Accept-Language`
- Browser tests also run on WebKit (Safari's engine), where most platform limitations come from
- The self-hosted package is tested in CI with its own store
- Test data never contains real notes

title: UI / UX
note:
- The UX concept is a separate document: [ux-concept.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/ux-concept.md)
- Accessible from the start: every component works with screen readers and keyboard only; every drag or gesture has an alternative (menu or keyboard command); sufficient contrast and scalable text
- Touch-first for phone and tablet: tap to select and tap again to edit ([D-91](item:1d5dd471-f0dd-585a-b54b-0d230106fb72)), drag-and-drop to move ([D-89](item:75a04881-7286-5ae6-b972-2db835c61de6)), indent and outdent from the editing toolbar and typing shortcuts ([D-54](item:f5b33fa9-57b5-5f10-9283-de9401068aa1), [D-75](item:22429d0b-c141-51ce-a505-3a9c1b858d99), [D-76](item:37604d09-f30d-59e2-bf20-57cee55994ec)); details in the UX concept
- Focus on any item as if it were its own document
- Breadcrumb for the current focus path
- Desktop add-on: keyboard shortcuts such as Enter (new sibling), Tab / Shift+Tab (indent/outdent), arrows (navigate), Ctrl+Up/Down (move)
- Tree switcher to move between the trees on a device
- An item shows which device last changed it and when, using the device label; the full change history per item is shown in the item's history ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)), since all events are kept
- Times are shown in the viewing device's local time; the original local time of the change (from the offset in the timestamp) can be shown as well, for example when a change was made while travelling
- Every tree is marked private or shared; a shared tree lists its users and their devices, and changes show the user as well as the device
- A short, plain explanation of what ThoughtTree protects and what it does not, shown when server sync is switched on and available at any time
- "Pair another device…" and "Share with another user" are two separate actions with separate wording and a warning before sharing
- UI state (collapsed items, current focus, open tree) belongs to one device: it is stored locally per tree and never synced; only domain events go into the event log

title: 9. Architecture Decisions
note: Each decision is a separate record in docs/adr. See the branches "Decisions (ADRs)" and "Open decisions"; release 1 scope is below.

title: Release 1 scope
note:
(decided by the owner, 2026-11-15; rules for agents in [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e) and [ADR-074](item:7c0c64b4-bde5-5bd3-b463-6fb08a445142), both Accepted)

Release 1 is the first public release. It gets the foundation right: everything it stores is final, so server sync, sharing, replicas and binary data can follow later without migrating data. Given by the owner: phone, tablet and desktop; no sync server, every device standalone, sync only by encrypted file with the guided round trip ([D-19](item:3751984b-f329-5796-9dc4-2434cdf36c72), [D-20](item:179e0e5b-74db-5dfe-a978-d4b147c04f03)); themes per tree and per item; the tutorial tree as the first tree; static hosting on Azure Static Web Apps with a preview per pull request ([D-50](item:65d2ce3c-705e-5bc9-a7ed-7b26e672e65a), [D-51](item:f3044799-1827-55a2-b744-add74418af04)).

| # | Decision | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Stored formats | Final from release 1: release 1 writes the server-ready envelope (encrypted payload wrapper, plaintext `EventId`, envelope version, `KeyId` and nonce, padding; the account id is authenticated data and not stored in the envelope) in the local store and the exchange file; later releases only add event types and fields ([ADR-016](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3)); format data starts with `tests/data/formats/1.0`. Encryption hardened before release 1 ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)): every plaintext header field (envelope version, `KeyId`, `EventId`) plus the account id and a fixed context label bound as additional authenticated data, `ServerSequence` excluded; the encrypted payload is a wrapper with room for optional parts (later device signatures without a new envelope version); daily use only through a non-extractable key handle, the raw key stored only wrapped by a non-extractable device key and unwrapped for pairing, sharing or backup (door for a later app lock); production keys and nonces only from the browser's cryptographic random source, checked by a test; snapshots, search index and drafts encrypted at rest with the tree key; the exchange file header holds only format version and `KeyId`, bound to the contents (the account id sits inside the encrypted part). Implementation notes: encryption runs through Web Crypto (AES-GCM is not available in .NET in the browser), calls are batched for replay; tests and simulation use .NET `AesGcm` against the same fixed test data. Considered and not taken: per-user keys or MLS (forward secrecy is meaningless for a readable history; revocation later by key rotation), XChaCha20-Poly1305 (not in Web Crypto), per-event derived keys (double cost; nonce safety secured by the random source test instead) |
| 2 | Pairing and sharing | Pairing own devices is in (the second device needs the key to read the exchange file). Sharing with other users is out; its formats and Domain rules are final and tested: `device.joined` with user identity, `user.name-changed`, `device.label-changed`, the code format with its own version and a kind (pairing or sharing), the derivation of private or shared |
| 3 | Features | **In (core):** outline (items, nesting, collapse, move, Focus, inbox [ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c), touch gestures and keyboard); several trees; device labels and who changed what; pairing, file round trip, visible conflicts ([ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d), [D-127](item:d80cde70-f754-5d09-8511-7c7e852a77bb)); undo with `actionId` on every event and item history ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0), [ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)); search on the device, across the open tree or the focused branch ([D-97](item:f5e08082-2869-5d7f-a753-3230c1ab1e25); searching all trees on the device, decided for release 1 on 2026-11-16, was moved to later by the owner on 2026-11-19, UX decision [D-186](item:84e4b048-39d7-5334-9e06-e1772e906858)); tags ([ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253)); relations ([ADR-024](item:ffd6a5a2-d9ad-5537-ba6f-456f67d962b2), [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2)); the connection map (a plain map of the relations between items: tap an item to highlight all its connections, tap a connected item to move there; not the atlas of [D-149](item:5e7dd59a-1ed1-5235-acba-a99a7d90aa17); core: release 1 does not ship without it, owner decision 2026-11-16); themes ([ADR-060](item:bf684b01-1e00-5613-b339-982fb1ed2313)); the tutorial, also in Easy language ([ADR-032](item:db1caf99-690c-5149-95de-09ad96b207b3), [D-146](item:9775a35a-5e71-5bf8-8c7f-fb84561f0363); owner decision 2026-11-16: in, as core); English and German; accessibility; export reminder ([D-126](item:8e2bb42e-d9dd-53d0-bd6b-7d7dbf1cecaf)); readable export (Markdown, OPML, JSON) and readable import; the Zettelkasten claim (owner decision 2026-11-18, [zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md)): Obsidian import and export with the round-trip guarantee G1 to G7, the update import ([ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e)), branch export and import from the thought's actions ([ADR-080](item:5512e2ce-cc4b-5c03-9cca-340487536507)), relation notes ([ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7)), the tree feature "Headings become thoughts" ([ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2)), tags and relation types named by untranslated titles ([ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2)), the map drawing links as untyped connections; the claim is made at release 1 when its acceptance scenarios pass; user-controlled updates ([ADR-036](item:7db9fef2-7ffe-5038-beb0-ca224f3a3da7)); feedback as GitHub issue, copy or file ([ADR-051](item:70d87940-8c95-593a-ba9d-aa3fd8631e22), [ADR-070](item:1a2c1cb0-92d0-5303-b72f-a0dc2733808d)); title: 11. Risks and Technical Debt
note:
- Blazor WASM startup size and initial load time, increased by loading the culture data for all languages
- Local store access from Blazor requires JS interop (IndexedDB; a Web Worker only if SQLite is ever adopted); performance for large logs needs measurement
- Event log growth: needs snapshotting and possibly compaction strategy
- Conflict rules for moves are non-trivial; need thorough tests
- Single developer: scope creep towards task management (the MLO trap)
- A shared key cannot be taken back: anyone who has received a tree's key keeps access to that tree
- Background sync in a PWA is limited: browsers decide themselves when periodic background sync runs, and some (Safari, iOS) do not support it; scheduled sync may only run while the app is open until a store app or package exists
- Multiple trees multiply the work: sync, search, snapshots and export all run per tree
- The browser may delete local data: Safari removes storage of sites not used for a while unless the app is installed to the home screen; mitigated by persistent storage, installing the PWA and regular export
- Losing every device that holds a tree loses the tree, because the server only holds ciphertext
- Hybrid clocks and replay order are easy to get subtly wrong; covered by property-based convergence tests
- Old app versions on rarely used devices skip newer events and may show an outdated tree until updated
- Authorship is not proven: anyone with a tree's key can write events that appear to come from another device or user; the server can withhold or replay events
- Membership only grows: devices and users cannot yet be removed from a tree, and device tokens do not expire
- A device with a clock far ahead, by mistake or on purpose in a shared tree, moves the clock of every device forward; last-writer-wins then stops following real time until real time catches up
- Live mode keeps connections open, which can prevent scaling to zero and raise cost; with several server replicas, in-memory rate limits and counters are per replica and reset on every cold start
- WCAG 2.2 AA is only partly verifiable automatically; screen reader experience relies on feedback
- Server data of accounts that are no longer used stays until account deletion and retention are decided
- LambdaTale is a niche dependency that every specification relies on ([ADR-075](item:43a28926-e5a3-53d3-a909-876064c319d6), bet card with review triggers)

title: 12. Glossary
note:
| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Outliner | Editor whose primary structure is a hierarchy of items rather than pages |
| Tree | One independent outline with its own key and event log; a device can hold several |
| Item | The thing in the tree: a title, an optional note, tags, and optionally a theme and views (later pictures and files); what it is (thought, idea, project, topic, vision) is up to the user, and an item can grow |
| Branch | An item together with everything below it |
| Node | Technical term only: how an item appears in the tree, its line and place; used in rendering and specifications |
| Title | The short text on an item's line |
| Thought | The user-facing word for an item in the texts the user reads ([D-140](item:4fec508f-8d98-5cf1-9104-57384c68e905)); documents and code say item |
| Note | The optional longer body of an item |
| Top-level Item | An item without a parent; a tree can have several |
| Parent / Children | The item directly above an item / the items directly below it |
| Sibling Order | The order of the children under one parent; follows from replaying the events, each placing an item after a named sibling |
| Hybrid Logical Clock | The clock carried by every event: one number in UTC milliseconds; it follows real time where possible and never goes back behind any event the device has seen, so events can be ordered the same way on every device |
| Conflict | Two or more changes with different values of the same field of an element (item, relation, relation type, tree feature, server address, view) made without seeing each other; shown to the user, who picks the value |
| Agreed Event Order | The order every device replays a tree's events in: by hybrid logical clock, then event id |
| Collapse | Hide an item's children in the view; UI state of one device, not a domain event |
| Focus | Make an item the temporary top of the view, showing its branch and the item as a page (title, tags, note; [D-151](item:768c4ff2-e921-5d89-9ef9-d0eed2cd469a), [ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)); "zoom" is used only for magnifying (pinch or browser zoom) |
| Event | Immutable record of one change to the tree |
| Event Log | The sequence of all events of one tree |
| Projection | The tree rebuilt by replaying events |
| Snapshot | A saved projection, used to speed up replay |
| App Ready | The moment the started app can show content, before the tree is loaded; app start is measured up to it (PF8, PF9), the tree from it (PF1) |
| Event Block | A local, rebuildable encrypted copy of about 1,000 events, used to speed up replay ([ADR-086](item:e4004cdd-2d5a-5579-b169-007f8d9fa1a7)) |
| Tombstone | Marker that an item was deleted without removing its data |
| User | A person who uses ThoughtTree, with a self-chosen name; a user can have several devices |
| Device | One installation of ThoughtTree, on a phone, tablet or desktop, belonging to one user |
| Device Label | The name of a device, such as "Tablet", shown next to the changes it made |
| Private Tree | A tree held only by devices of one user |
| Shared Tree | A tree held by devices of more than one user |
| Pairing | Bringing a tree onto another device of the same user, via QR code or typed code |
| Sharing | Giving a tree to another user by handing over its key and account identity; every user of a shared tree can read and change all of it |
| Key | The end-to-end encryption key of one tree; exists only on devices that hold that tree |
| Account | The identity of one tree towards the sync server (account id and account secret); one account per tree; not a user account: there are no user accounts or logins on the server |
| Account Secret | Secret created on the device with a tree; proves to the sync server that a device may join that tree's account |
| Device Token | Credential that lets a device access a tree's event log on the sync server |
| Event Envelope | The stored and transmitted form of an event: a few plaintext fields plus the encrypted payload |
| Upcasting | Converting an event written in an older schema version to the current shape when it is read |
| Sync Transport | The way events travel between devices (`ISyncTransport`): through the server or as an export file |
| Export File | An encrypted file containing a tree's events, used for device-to-device sync and as a backup |
| Readable Export | An unencrypted Markdown, OPML or JSON file with the current tree, without history |
| Release Flag | A temporary switch, shipped with the app, that keeps an unfinished feature off in an environment |
| Experiment Flag | A switch that gives a feature to a share of accounts, to learn whether it works; ends with the review of its bet card |
| Operations Flag | A long-lived server switch that turns something off quickly if it causes trouble (kill switch) |
| Permission Flag | A flag per account on the server that says what the account may do |
| Bet | An architecture decision that rests on an assumption; its bet card says what should improve, how we notice it and when we review it |
| Tree Feature | A feature the user switches on or off for a tree, recorded as an event so all devices of the tree agree |
| View | A saved perspective of an item's branch or the whole tree: a name, a query and a layout |
| Inbox | The item of a tree where captured thoughts wait to be placed; always shown last at the top level |
| Template | An item marked as a template; creating from it copies its branch, valid in its parent's branch |
| Tag | An item inside the tree's Tags branch, named by its title, that items can carry in any number; typed with `@@` or chosen in the tag picker |
| PWA | Progressive Web App: installable, offline-capable web application |
| Installation | The app as loaded from one server (the hosted service or a self-hosted one), with its own local store and trees; it syncs only with that server |
| Tree Access | What a device needs outside the event log to read and sync a tree: key, `KeyId`, account id, account secret |
| User Identity | User id and user name of a person; carried to their other devices by pairing |
| Tree Name | The title of the first visible top-level item other than the inbox (and the Tags and Relation types branches, [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2)) |
| `EventId` | Globally unique id of an event; readable in the envelope; the same id must always carry the same content (INV-13) |
| `KeyId` | Short random id of a tree's key, readable in the envelope |
| `ServerSequence` | Gap-free number the server gives each envelope of an account, in commit order; used only to track sync progress |
| `reverts` | Event id of the change an undo event reverts |
| `actionId` | Id shared by all events written for one user action; quick undo reverts an action as one step |
| `replaces` | List of event ids of the changes an event replaces; used to detect conflicts |
| `seen` | For each device of a tree, the highest clock a device had received from it; carried by `item.deleted`, `item.exported` and `tree.exported` |
| Envelope / Schema / App Version | Version of the stored envelope format / of one event type's shape / of the installed release |
| Padding Bucket | One of the fixed sizes a payload is padded to before encryption |
| Join Code | Code an operator hands out so that accounts can register on a server in "join code only" mode |
| Sync Mode | Live, manual or scheduled; chosen per tree and device |
| Relation / Relation Type | A typed, directed connection between two items of a tree / its type, an item inside the tree's Relation types branch |
| `item:` Link | A Markdown link to an item of the same tree by its id |
| Backlink | A link or incoming relation shown on the item it points to |
| Draft | Text being edited, saved locally until it becomes an event at the end of the editing session |
| Gate / Watch | A test result that stops delivery on a single failure / a measure that is tracked over time |
| Invariant | A core rule of the domain with an id (INV-n), checked by property tests |
| Reference Model | A deliberately naive projection that serves as the referee for the real one |
| Regression Seed | A simulation seed that failed once and is replayed on every push |
| Specify / Secure / Confirm | The three intents of tests: acceptance criteria / correctness and rules / the whole system in real environments |
| Inner Loop / Branch Check / Push Gate | Tests an agent runs while working / the smaller set CI runs on every push to a branch / the full set that must pass before a change can merge (runs on pull requests) |
| Spec Host | A test build of the client with hooks to load state and control time, never shipped |
| Test Id Catalogue | Shared C# constants naming the `data-testid` of every element that shows a domain concept |
| Bet Card | The entry for a bet in `docs/adr/bets.md`: TL;DR, outcome, assumption, signal, review trigger |
| Diagnostics Block / Usage Summary | Numbers and switch states added to feedback / counts computed on the device from one tree the user chooses |
| Feedback Inbox / Operator | The server's optional inbox for feedback encrypted to the operator / the person who runs a server |
| MLO | MyLifeOrganized, the task outliner whose UI inspired ThoughtTree |

title: 📜 Decisions (ADRs)
note: All 89 architecture decision records, grouped by area. Each note holds the rules and the reason; bets carry their bet card. Format: [docs/adr/README.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md).

title: Events and stored data
note: Event log, event shapes, ordering, storage and the formats release 1 freezes

title: ADR-002 Event sourcing as data model
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** record every change of a tree's content as an immutable event
- **MUST** derive the tree only by replaying events (projection)
- **MUST NOT** store, sync or export tree state as the source of truth; snapshots are local caches that can be thrown away

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-002"
```

why: Enables offline-first work and log-based sync with small, mergeable changes.

Source: [ADR-002-event-sourcing.md](item:92164dbe-21ee-55af-bc65-472f8ec4a151)

title: ADR-004 Sibling order by reference
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

Rules 4 and 5 added by owner decision 2026-11-26.

- **MUST** place an item by `afterItemId` (empty: first child, or first at top level)
- **MUST NOT** store order keys, indices or positions on items or in events
- **MUST** place an item first under its parent if the referenced sibling is under another parent at replay time; deleted siblings stay resolvable as tombstones
- **MUST NOT** apply a move whose parent or `afterItemId` does not exist at that point of the replay, or whose `afterItemId` is the item itself; the item stays where it was and the move is reported
- **MUST** place a new item whose parent does not exist at that point of the replay at top level, and one whose `afterItemId` does not exist or is the item itself first under its parent; both are reported

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-004"
```

why: The order follows from replaying the log; no growing keys.

Source: [ADR-004-sibling-order-by-reference.md](item:0ccf02fa-ad37-5336-ac82-a0bd90837e40)

title: ADR-005 Tombstones instead of hard deletes
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** mark deleted items as deleted (tombstone) and keep their data, children and relations
- **MUST NOT** physically remove items or events

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-005"
```

why: Deterministic merges; restore and undo stay possible.

title: ADR-009 Merging is the union of logs; no special root
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

- **MUST** merge by taking the union of event logs, identified by `EventId`
- **MUST NOT** merge projections or trees directly
- **MUST** treat an item without parent as a top-level item; a tree may have several
- **MUST NOT** introduce a root item, a fixed root id or any item not created by `item.created`
- **MUST** take the tree name from the title of the first visible top-level item other than the inbox ([ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c)), with no event of its own

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-009"
```

why: One merge rule for server sync and file sync of devices that hold the same tree; trees of devices that started on their own are brought together only by importing a tree into another ([ADR-010](item:d516ce73-4cb1-5400-a5ce-f72a42b37e1a)).

Source: [ADR-009-merge-is-union.md](item:b0e72d5b-1912-510c-bc12-0663d1cef1a3)

title: ADR-014 Event order by hybrid logical clock
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

Rewritten by owner decision 2026-11-25: the clock is one number (was UTC time plus a counter) and the event id breaks ties (was the device id).

- **MUST** order events for replay by `clock`, then `EventId` compared as text, ordinal
- **MUST** give a new event the clock `max(now, highest + 1)`: `now` is the device's UTC time in milliseconds, `highest` the highest clock in the tree's log
- **MUST** give a new event the largest clock value if the log already holds it; the event id then orders it
- **MUST** derive the clock from the local log; MUST NOT store it separately
- **MUST** accept events from clocks far ahead and warn; MUST NOT reject or cap them
- **MUST** apply every event that ties on `clock`; MUST NOT drop, reject or report an event for the tie alone
- **MUST NOT** use `timestamp`, arrival order or sequence numbers to decide order or conflicts, nor `deviceId` to decide order
- **MUST NOT** change this order in a later app version

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-014"
```

why: Every device computes the same tree; a change always sorts after everything its device had seen, and the latest edit in real time usually wins.

Source: [ADR-014-hybrid-logical-clock.md](item:9df73033-049e-5697-be5c-13b64887d885)

title: ADR-016 Downward-compatible event versioning
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

Amended by [ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a) (formats may change before release 1; the rules bind stored data from release 1 on); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST NOT** change or rewrite a stored event; only its envelope may be re-encrypted
- **MUST** only add fields to existing events; MUST NOT remove a field or change its meaning
- **MUST** express structure only through the basic events (`item.created`, `item.moved`, `item.deleted`, `item.restored`, `item.title-changed`, `item.note-changed`)
- **MUST** put new kinds of information into new event types
- **MUST** treat a missing field as "unchanged", never as "reset to default"
- **MUST** store, sync and skip unknown events, keep the tree editable and show a warning
- **MUST** rebuild snapshots and search index when the app version changes

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-016"
git diff --diff-filter=DM origin/main...HEAD -- tests/data/formats | wc -l   # expect 0; runs on every pull request against its base
```

why: Devices run different app versions; older devices must never miss items or texts.

Source: [ADR-016-downward-compatible-events.md](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3)

title: ADR-017 JSON with fixed type names
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

- **MUST** serialize events as JSON inside the encrypted payload
- **MUST** use fixed type names such as `item.created`
- **MUST NOT** derive type names from .NET type or member names

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-017"
```

title: ADR-022 Binary data as separate blobs
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST NOT** put binary data (pictures, files) inside events
- **MUST** store binary data, once supported, as separate encrypted blobs referenced by id

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-022"
```

why: Events are replayed, synced and kept forever and padded for small sizes.

Source: [ADR-022-binary-blobs.md](item:4bb51fd5-b1a6-503d-9a52-d8f9caf33887)

title: ADR-023 One parent per item
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

Rule 3 changed by owner decision 2026-11-26 (was: place the item at top level).

- **MUST** give every item at most one parent
- **MUST NOT** implement clones or items in several places; use links or relations instead
- **MUST NOT** apply a move that would put an item under itself or one of its descendants; the item stays where it was and the move is reported

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-023"
```

why: Moves, cycle checks, delete conflicts, sibling order, focus path and export rely on one parent.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that links and relations are enough, so nobody misses having the same item in several places.

- **Outcome:** The tree model stays simple: moves, cycle checks, deletion, conflicts, order, focus path and export all rely on a single parent.
- **Assumption:** When someone wants something in two places, a link or relation, together with backlinks, meets that need.
- **Signal:** Feedback asking for clones, mirrors or "the same item in two places"; answers to "Have you wanted the same item in two places?" (no / sometimes / often); in the usage summary, the number of links and relations per 100 items.
- **Review when:** repeated feedback asks for clones · importing from other outliners loses information because the source uses clones.

Source: [ADR-023-one-parent.md](item:4da40799-3f96-5b48-b124-3848e7ed2711)

title: ADR-029 Text normalisation before writing
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2) (headings in notes depend on the tree feature "Headings become thoughts") and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (display names no longer exist); owner decisions 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** normalise all text to Unicode NFC before it enters an event (titles, notes, display names, names) (amended by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): there are no display names)
- **MUST** store line breaks in notes as `\n`; replace line breaks in titles by spaces
- **MUST** normalise again in search and comparisons
- **MUST** store titles as single-line Markdown with inline formatting and notes as Markdown without headings ([ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)), with `format: markdown` (amended by [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2): with the tree feature "Headings become thoughts" off, headings stay in the note)

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-029"
```

why: Events are never rewritten; mixed forms would break search, comparisons and conflicts forever.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that Markdown is the right text format: simple to store, search and export, and comfortable enough to edit on a phone.

- **Outcome:** Titles and notes stay plain text with light formatting; search, conflicts, readable export and downward compatibility stay simple; the editor can improve later without changing stored data.
- **Assumption:** People can write Markdown on a phone, or an editor that shows formatting directly makes it comfortable; inline formatting in titles is wanted and does not get in the way of quick capture.
- **Signal:** Feedback about editing and formatting; answers to "How is formatting text on your phone?" (easy / okay / annoying); in the usage summary, the share of titles and of notes with Markdown, and how often formatting is applied by toolbar versus typed.
- **Review when:** repeated feedback calls formatting on the phone annoying · Markdown in titles is hardly used · a good touch editor is only available as a JavaScript library (same trigger as [ADR-001](item:b1e9b6bd-456d-5225-b054-3feb752f7206); both bets are reviewed together).

Source: [ADR-029-text-normalisation.md](item:60a30705-4e16-547f-9365-4d928fe34dc1)

title: ADR-038 Local storage migrations without loss
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a) (the local store layout may change before release 1; the rules bind from release 1 on); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** give the local store layout (IndexedDB or SQLite) a version and migrate it step by step on upgrade
- **MUST NOT** delete or overwrite events or tree access during a migration; a failed migration leaves the old data untouched
- **MUST** test every migration in real browsers: a database created by the previous release is opened by the new one and nothing is missing

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-038"   # end-to-end migration tests
```

why: A failed migration loses notes that may exist on no other device.

Source: [ADR-038-local-storage-migration.md](item:431e9c69-ea9d-566d-8817-d56981f08506)

title: ADR-085 Beta data before release 1
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

Amends [ADR-016](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3) and [ADR-038](item:431e9c69-ea9d-566d-8817-d56981f08506) (they bind stored data from release 1 on); owner decision 2026-11-19 (session "Tags and relation types as items"), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MAY** change stored formats (events, envelope, local store layout) before release 1; from release 1 on [ADR-016](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3) and [ADR-038](item:431e9c69-ea9d-566d-8817-d56981f08506) apply without exception
- **MUST** give every build before release 1 a stored-format version and keep it with each tree on the device
- **MUST**, before an update that changes the stored-format version, tell the tester so and offer to export every tree in the Obsidian form ([zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md)); the update waits until the tester has exported or declined ([ADR-036](item:7db9fef2-7ffe-5038-beb0-ca224f3a3da7))
- **MUST**, after such an update, keep the old trees' data untouched, show them as not readable by this version, and offer to import the exported files as new trees (a copy; history, conflicts and devices are lost)
- **MUST NOT** promise testers that their data survives; the prompt says "kept as far as possible"; the prompt and the import offer are new UI and need a sketch first ([ADR-064](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-085"
```

why: Formats must stay free to change while testers use the app before release 1; the Obsidian form is the most stable bridge, since its conventions are not ours and it carries everything but history (owner: "should not lose data on the way to v1, if possible, but it is not guaranteed").

Source: [ADR-085-beta-data-before-release-1.md](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a)

title: ADR-086 Local event blocks for replay
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Owner decision 2026-11-25 (spike 1 decision 4, option A), accepted by the owner 2026-11-25 after reviewing the text. Meets the "SHOULD batch Web Crypto calls during replay" rule of [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e); amends no ADR. Part of the local store layout ([ADR-074](item:7c0c64b4-bde5-5bd3-b463-6fb08a445142)), versioned by [ADR-038](item:431e9c69-ea9d-566d-8817-d56981f08506) and free to change before release 1 ([ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a)).

- **MUST** keep the per-event envelopes as the source of truth; blocks are a local copy that can be rebuilt from them at any time
- **MUST NOT** sync, export or send blocks to a server; sync and the envelope format stay unchanged
- **MUST** also store a tree's events locally in encrypted blocks of about 1,000 events
- **MUST** encrypt a block with the tree key only through the non-extractable key handle ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)), binding as additional authenticated data a fixed context label for blocks, the tree id, the account id, the `KeyId`, the block's event range and the local store layout version
- **MUST** pad a block's plaintext to a multiple of 16 KiB
- **MUST** treat an event as saved once its envelope is stored ([ADR-088](item:1b0c1552-bab4-544f-a638-26aec44b401e)); writing the block that holds it never delays this
- **MUST** replay from the blocks plus the events not yet in a block, giving the same tree as a replay from the envelopes alone
- **MUST** rebuild a missing, unreadable or incomplete block from the envelopes; a broken block never prevents the start
- **MAY** discard and rebuild all blocks, for example after a layout migration

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-086"
```

why: Spike 1 measured that one read and one Web Crypto call per event dominate a full replay (phone, Chrome: read and decrypt 11.6 s with one call each per event against 1.2 s in blocks of 1,000; replay from blocks estimated at 5 to 6 s); as derived data the blocks cost only local storage (about 70 % more, report estimate) and leave the stored server-ready formats unchanged.

Source: [ADR-086-local-event-blocks.md](item:e4004cdd-2d5a-5579-b169-007f8d9fa1a7)

title: ADR-087 Stored size limits
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Sets the numbers left open by [ADR-015](item:0a4a5821-6c8b-5175-936c-4ba123adbdc3) (padding to a size bucket) and [ADR-028](item:510c155f-f2a3-5463-ac8d-0643a54f3e35) (name and address maximums); amends no rule. Owner decision 2026-11-25 (spike 1 decision 6), accepted by the owner 2026-11-25; user name and address limits changed by the owner the same day after the independent review (largest code against the QR size, [ADR-028](item:510c155f-f2a3-5463-ac8d-0643a54f3e35)), as was the padding scope (event payloads only).

- **MUST** pad every event payload of an envelope before encryption to the smallest of the buckets 512 B, 1 KiB, 2 KiB, 4 KiB, 8 KiB and 16 KiB that holds it, and a payload above 16 KiB to a multiple of 16 KiB; encrypted local-only data follows its own rules (event blocks: [ADR-086](item:e4004cdd-2d5a-5579-b169-007f8d9fa1a7)) and is not padded otherwise (snapshots, drafts, search index)
- **MUST** limit a note to 50,000 characters and a title to 1,000 characters, enforced when an event is written
- **MUST** limit a user name to 32 characters and a server address to 100 ASCII characters (an international domain name in its ASCII form), and put one tree into a pairing code
- **MUST** count characters as Unicode code points after normalisation ([ADR-029](item:60a30705-4e16-547f-9365-4d928fe34dc1)), the same on every device; the UI MAY show a count closer to what the user sees
- **MUST** enforce these limits in the UI as well: no input beyond a limit is accepted
- **MUST** tell the user when a limit is reached, and for a note also when it gets close; the form (counter, message, paste beyond the limit) is new UI and needs a sketch first ([ADR-064](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d))
- **MAY** raise a maximum in a later release; **MUST NOT** lower one, because stored data may already reach it

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-087"
```

why: The numbers become stored formats with release 1; spike 1 measured 31.5 % padding overhead for these buckets against 137.6 % for the provisional list, notes up to 50,000 characters on the phone, and a pairing code that fits QR version 15 at level M even for the largest name (32 code points of 4 bytes: about 354 bytes, estimated from the spike's layout, which fits 363 bytes at version 15); raising later is safe, lowering is not.

Source: [ADR-087-stored-size-limits.md](item:0fbcadf7-3838-57a9-a1d6-07178194dfbb)

title: ADR-088 When a local write counts as saved
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Owner decision 2026-11-25 (spike 1 decision 8, option B), accepted by the owner 2026-11-25; test rule, why line and the scope of `strict` (every store not listed as `relaxed`) changed by the owner the same day after the independent review; amends no ADR.

- **MUST** treat an event as saved (shown as saved, its draft cleared, its undo step recorded) only after the transaction that stores its envelope reports `complete`
- **MUST** write every local store with `strict` durability where the browser offers the setting, unless it is listed in the next rule; this covers events, tree access, device token, sync progress, the layout version, device settings and any new store
- **MAY** write only these rebuildable or short-lived stores with `relaxed` durability: snapshots, event blocks, search index, drafts, UI state
- **MUST** secure this with end-to-end scenario 8: after the app is killed while writing, no saved event is lost, no batch is half visible and the store opens; push gate in Chromium, nightly in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-088"
```

why: No data loss is quality goal 1; only `strict` covers an OS crash or power loss, which cannot be tested. Spike 1 found 0 losses in 940 desktop kills or closes and 20 phone swipe-aways, but only 200 desktop Chromium kills ran with `strict` (the rest with the browser default); there `strict` cost about 13 % write throughput. Editing writes events at the end of an editing session, so the cost is small there, while drafts written on every keystroke stay fast; the cost for imports, which write many events at once, is not measured (open decision "Durability of imports").

Source: [ADR-088-write-acknowledgement.md](item:1b0c1552-bab4-544f-a638-26aec44b401e)

title: Sync and exchange
note: How devices exchange events: by file, through the server, and in which modes

title: ADR-003 Own ASP.NET Core sync service
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** implement the sync service in ASP.NET Core
- **MUST NOT** depend on a backend-as-a-service (Firebase, Supabase, Appwrite, …)
- **SHOULD** keep the server a thin store and relay of encrypted envelopes

verify:

```bash
grep -riE 'firebase|supabase|appwrite' --include=*.csproj src | wc -l   # expect 0
```

why: Full control over the event model and merge rules; stays in .NET; self-hostable.

Source: [ADR-003-own-sync-service.md](item:3cb519f6-10f0-52d2-a150-4c9bd6b514f2)

title: ADR-006 Event exchange behind ISyncTransport
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** exchange events with server or file only through `ISyncTransport`
- **MUST** follow the four steps: find out what the other side has, send what it lacks, receive what this side lacks, skip duplicates by `EventId`
- **MUST** deliver the events of a device without gaps: never a later event of device D without all earlier ones
- **MUST** track sync progress per destination, not by one synced flag per event
- **MUST** store each `EventId` only once on the server, so repeated pushes are harmless
- **MUST** reject an envelope whose `EventId` is known but whose content differs, on the server and on every device, and report it as a defect (INV-13)
- **MUST** give `ServerSequence` numbers gap-free per account and make them readable only in commit order
- **MUST** store a pushed batch all or nothing, in the order sent; **MUST** send batches strictly one after another, each only after the previous one is confirmed

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-006"
```

why: One exchange rule for every transport; conflict detection relies on the no-gap rule.

Source: [ADR-006-event-exchange.md](item:34effd99-9156-51ff-86f7-a97e805a72d8)

title: ADR-007 Device-to-device sync by encrypted file
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

- **MUST** export the whole encrypted log by default; import by merging with duplicates skipped
- **MUST** give the export file its own format version and a header with only the format version and `KeyId` ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)); optional parts go inside the encrypted part
- **SHOULD** offer an incremental export later, based on what the other device had at its last import

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-007"
```

why: Must work without internet; doubles as a backup.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that manual sync by file is worth offering, because some users can't or won't use a server.

- **Outcome:** Devices sync without internet and without any server; the export file doubles as a backup.
- **Assumption:** People without a usable server (no internet, VPNs blocked, privacy concerns) accept a manual step (export, hand over, import) and really use it.
- **Signal:** Your own use; feedback about file sync; answers to "How do your devices sync?" (server / file / both / not at all); in the usage summary, the number of file imports in the last 30 days.
- **Review when:** a store app or package with automatic discovery on the local network exists · feedback says the manual steps are too cumbersome · among the first 20 answers to the question, nobody answers "file".

Source: [ADR-007-file-sync.md](item:72d8232b-5c71-5140-9596-9e03184d4407)

title: ADR-021 Server address is a property of the tree
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** record the tree's server address, and its join code if any, by `tree.server-changed`
- **MUST** sync a tree with a server only from the installation loaded from that server; in any other installation, the tree syncs by file only and the app names the right installation
- **MUST** move a tree to another server by pairing it into that server's installation and switching server sync on there
- **MUST** keep whether a device uses the server, and its sync mode, on the device
- **MAY** include the server address and join code in the pairing and sharing code

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-021"   # when: server
```

why: All devices of a tree must meet on the same server; one installation per server keeps the Content Security Policy strict.

Source: [ADR-021-server-address-event.md](item:1bed8f67-f627-544b-9315-d787fb72e46d)

title: ADR-037 Versioned, compatible sync API
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** carry the API version in the address (`/v1/…`)
- **MUST** keep the server able to serve every released client version of the same major API version
- **MUST** let the client work with older servers, or tell the user clearly that the server needs updating
- **MUST** add recorded requests and responses of each release to `tests/data/formats/<version>/`
- **MUST NOT** change the meaning of an existing endpoint, field or status code within a major version

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-037"
```

why: Self-hosted servers and apps update independently; an unversioned API cannot get versioning later without breaking clients.

Source: [ADR-037-api-versioning.md](item:6b2c2a7e-542e-5ef5-aacf-272cf9336ea1)

title: ADR-057 Sync modes, live preselected
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** offer live, manual and scheduled sync per tree and device
- **MUST** let the user choose the mode when server sync is switched on, with live preselected and the trade-offs explained
- **MUST** show unsynced changes and remind the user in manual and scheduled mode after a time the user sets

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-057"   # when: server
```

why: Reliability comes first; users who care more about activity patterns can still choose manual or scheduled sync.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that reliability matters more to users than hiding activity patterns, so live sync is preselected, while manual and scheduled remain available.

- **Outcome:** Changes reach other devices quickly and are not lost because they never left a device; users who care more about activity patterns can choose manual or scheduled sync.
- **Assumption:** Most users prefer automatic sync and accept that the server sees when they are online; users of manual or scheduled sync notice the indicator and reminder and do not lose changes.
- **Signal:** Feedback about sync and lost changes; answers to "Have you ever lost changes that weren't synced?" (no / once / more than once) and "Which sync mode do you use?" (live / manual / scheduled); in the usage summary, the sync mode in use and the number of reminders about unsynced changes in the last 30 days.
- **Review when:** users of manual or scheduled sync report lost changes · many users switch from live to manual · the store app or package exists, so reliable background sync could make scheduled sync the better default.

Source: [ADR-057-sync-modes.md](item:689ca80b-6bc9-5539-b87d-4fbbc9269055)

title: Trees, devices and sharing
note: Standalone devices, several trees, pairing, sharing, keys and tree access

title: ADR-008 Standalone first
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** create key and account identity of a tree on the device
- **MUST** work fully with no network, server, account or login
- **MUST NOT** require the server for anything except server sync

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-008"
```

why: A device must work on its own; server sync is optional per tree.

Source: [ADR-008-standalone-first.md](item:7029c997-8bb9-5497-aef3-c77a8913c123)

title: ADR-010 Multiple independent trees per device
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** partition all local data by tree id: events, snapshots, tree access, device token, search index, settings
- **MUST NOT** share keys, events or indexes between trees; copies (copy and paste, [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e); readable export and import, [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)) create new items and connect nothing; the only exception is importing a whole tree into another as a new branch, which adds its events to the target tree's log, re-encrypted with the target's key, followed by events that keep the target's name, theme and inbox

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-010"
```

why: Separate trees and sharing one tree without exposing the others.

Source: [ADR-010-multiple-trees.md](item:d516ce73-4cb1-5400-a5ce-f72a42b37e1a)

title: ADR-011 Pairing and sharing are separate
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** keep pairing (own devices) and sharing (other users) as separate actions, with a warning before sharing
- **MUST** include the user identity in the pairing code; MUST NOT include it in the sharing code
- **MUST** write `device.joined` as the first event of a new tree and whenever a device joins
- **MUST** derive private or shared from `device.joined` events (latest per device counts); MUST NOT store it as a flag
- **MUST** apply `device.label-changed` to the device that wrote it, and `user.name-changed` only if the writing device joined with that `userId`; ignore it otherwise
- **MUST** ask, when a device with another user identity adopts one by pairing, whether both are the same person; if so write a new `device.joined` in each of its trees

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-011"
```

why: Shows where changes come from and whether a tree is private or shared.

Source: [ADR-011-pairing-and-sharing.md](item:7d7604de-3eb6-5062-8d09-4e59ca7f43c0)

title: ADR-012 One key per tree, equal access
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

- **MUST** use one random key per tree, the same for every holder
- **MUST NOT** implement read-only roles, per-user keys or revocation (deferred)
- **MUST** use the key in daily use only as a non-extractable handle and store the raw key only wrapped; unwrap it only for pairing, sharing or key backup (amended by [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-012"
```

why: Keeps the encryption design simple; per-user keys are a much larger design.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that one simple shared key is enough, because people share trees rarely and only with people they trust.

- **Outcome:** Encryption stays simple and robust; sharing works offline with one code.
- **Assumption:** Sharing is rare and only with trusted people; nobody needs read-only access or to take access back; when trust ends, starting a new tree and moving the content by readable export and import is acceptable.
- **Signal:** Feedback asking for read-only access or revocation; answers to "Have you ever wanted to take back access to a shared tree?" (no / yes, once / yes, often); in the usage summary, the number of trees and of shared trees on the device (counts only, no activity of shared trees).
- **Review when:** the first feedback asking for read-only access or revocation arrives · a shared key is known to have leaked · sharing with larger groups (more than a few people) becomes a real use case.

Source: [ADR-012-one-key-per-tree.md](item:33bd5096-18d5-5fa9-9dc1-c959db5793be)

title: ADR-013 Device state is never synced
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** save text being edited as a local draft on every change and turn it into an event at the end of the editing session or after a crash
- **MUST** keep collapsed items, focus, open tree, language, sync mode, use of the server and experimental-features switch on the device, per tree where applicable
- **MUST NOT** write device state into the event log
- The theme of a tree or item is content, not device state ([ADR-060](item:bf684b01-1e00-5613-b339-982fb1ed2313)); device settings such as the hand side stay on the device

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-013"
```

why: The log records content changes; each device keeps its own view.

Source: [ADR-013-device-local-state.md](item:2503cff6-630e-5fbd-89f6-22dd074fee11)

title: ADR-020 No user accounts on the server
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** authenticate only by device tokens, one per device and tree
- **MUST NOT** add user accounts or logins (OpenID Connect, OAuth, …)

verify:

```bash
grep -rE 'AddOpenIdConnect|AddMicrosoftIdentity|AddOAuth' src | wc -l   # expect 0
```

why: A login would link all trees of a user to one identity on the server.

Source: [ADR-020-no-server-accounts.md](item:0d048d05-14df-5253-a1ec-9d6028df752b)

title: ADR-028 Tree access
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

- **MUST** keep key, `KeyId`, account id and account secret (the tree access) outside the event log, stored only by the Tree Manager
- **MUST** hand over exactly the tree access in pairing, sharing and key backup; pairing adds the user identity
- **MUST NOT** put tree access, device tokens or device settings into events
- **MUST** give the pairing and sharing code its own format version
- **MUST** limit the length of user name and server address so that the largest possible code fits into a QR code that phones read reliably
- **MUST** keep Crypto stateless: the key handle (non-extractable, [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)) is handed in for each operation

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-028"
```

why: The log restores content, the tree access restores the right to read and sync it.

Source: [ADR-028-tree-access.md](item:510c155f-f2a3-5463-ac8d-0643a54f3e35)

title: ADR-069 Copy and paste between trees
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253) and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (tags and relation types are items, matched by title); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** let the user copy items with their branches and paste them into another tree (or another place of the same tree)
- **MUST** create the pasted items with new ids, as one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)), so one undo removes the whole paste
- **MUST** carry over titles, notes, format, structure, tags (matched by title in the target tree, created there as items in the Tags branch when missing; amended by [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253): tags are items; amended by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): relation types are matched by title in the same way), themes and template markings
- **MUST** rewrite `item:` links and relations within the copied branches to the copies; **MUST** drop relations to items outside them and leave such links as they are (shown as not found in another tree)
- **MUST NOT** carry over history, devices or authorship: a paste starts fresh, like a readable import
- **MUST** also put Markdown and formatted text on the system clipboard, so pasting into other apps works (UX decision [D-61](item:3d4b82a1-e252-59f6-8375-d2611145d205))
- **MUST** show a calm hint the first time content is pasted into a shared tree ("This tree is shared with …")

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-069"
```

why: Copies move content between trees without connecting them; templates and any other branch can be reused across trees.

Source: [ADR-069-copy-paste-between-trees.md](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e)

title: Security and privacy
note: Encryption, metadata protection and what the server and printed output may see

title: ADR-015 Minimal plaintext in the envelope
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** keep only `EventId`, envelope version, `KeyId` (a short random id assigned when the key is created), nonce and `ServerSequence` in plaintext
- **MUST** encrypt the payload wrapper that holds the event ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)) with AES-GCM (256-bit key, fresh random nonce per envelope), binding every plaintext field except the nonce and `ServerSequence`, plus the account id and a fixed context label, as additional authenticated data (amended by [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e); the account id is authenticated but not stored in the envelope)
- **MUST** pad the payload to a size bucket before encryption
- **MUST NOT** add a plaintext field without a new ADR

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-015"
```

why: The server only stores, deduplicates and relays; anything more would reveal structure or activity.

Source: [ADR-015-envelope-plaintext.md](item:0a4a5821-6c8b-5175-936c-4ba123adbdc3)

title: ADR-030 Metadata protection
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST NOT** store receive times or IP addresses on the server, or record IP addresses in logs
- **MUST** push events in batches after a pause in editing
- **MUST** send a neutral `Accept-Language` header with sync requests
- **MUST** run scheduled sync at a random moment within a window fixed in UTC
- **MUST NOT** add analytics, telemetry or third-party requests to the client or the server (the server writes plain logs only); user-initiated feedback encrypted to the operator ([ADR-055](item:faf555b0-b43a-58c1-bdd7-c1e0a73c91a3)) is not telemetry

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-030"
```

why: Nobody operating or observing the server should learn where the user is or how they work.

Source: [ADR-030-metadata-protection.md](item:68a5428c-3b63-557c-b2c1-4957cf63343a)

title: ADR-043 Server secrets only as hashes
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** store account secrets, device tokens and join codes only as hashes
- **MUST** compare them in constant time
- **MUST NOT** log secrets, tokens or join codes

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-043"   # when: server
```

why: Stolen server data must not let anyone join an account or push events.

Source: [ADR-043-hashed-server-secrets.md](item:7dada8b0-0f86-546b-960a-339efd10fa38)

title: ADR-044 Abuse protection and registration modes
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`

- **MUST** enforce a maximum request size and maximum events and storage per account
- **MUST** rate-limit registrations and requests in memory only; **MUST NOT** store the IP addresses used for it
- **MUST** support the registration modes "open" and "join code only", set per server
- **MUST** reject oversized or malformed requests without storing them
- **MAY** keep server counters (rejected registrations, rate-limit hits, accounts, storage used): counts only, no IP addresses or account ids, in memory or as daily totals, visible only to the operator

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-044"   # when: server
```

why: Without user accounts anyone can register; limits keep a server, and its free tier, from being abused.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that open registration would be abused, so the owner's server requires a join code, while limits protect servers that stay open.

- **Outcome:** Strangers cannot fill the owner's server and its free tier; self-hosters choose between open and join code.
- **Assumption:** Abuse of an open server is likely enough that the extra step is worth it; the step barely bothers legitimate users, because the join code travels in the pairing code.
- **Signal:** Feedback about trouble joining a server; Azure costs; server counters: rejected registrations (missing or wrong join code), rate-limit hits, number of accounts and storage used.
- **Review when:** Azure costs rise or the free tier is exceeded · many rejected registrations show someone probing · feedback says joining is too hard · the owner wants to offer a public, open server.

Source: [ADR-044-abuse-protection.md](item:34ee2980-e31e-51ca-ba0f-7404c17260fc)

title: ADR-045 Strict Content Security Policy
note:
applies_to: `src/**`, `infra/**`

- **MUST** serve the app with a strict Content Security Policy: scripts, styles, fonts, images and connections only to its own origin, which is also its sync server (one installation per server, [ADR-021](item:1bed8f67-f627-544b-9315-d787fb72e46d))
- **MUST** send `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`
- **MUST NOT** fetch link previews automatically
- **MUST NOT** load anything from third parties (trackers, fonts, analytics, remote pictures in Markdown)
- **MUST** send the policy as HTTP headers on every hosting (Azure Static Web Apps configuration file in release 1, the server later), not only as a page tag
- **MUST** let a self-hosted package serve its own app with its own policy, instead of widening the policy of the hosted app
- **MUST NOT** weaken the policy with `unsafe-inline` or `unsafe-eval` beyond what Blazor WebAssembly requires (`wasm-unsafe-eval`)

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-045"   # headers in deployment and end-to-end tests; when: after deployment
```

why: The browser itself blocks every request to third parties, whatever code creeps in.

Source: [ADR-045-strict-csp.md](item:4ed194a5-683a-5f25-9867-341f6922bd57)

title: ADR-052 Content is untrusted input
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

Amended by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (display names no longer exist); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** treat all content (titles, notes, imported files, feedback texts) as untrusted, also in the owner's own trees
- **MUST** render Markdown without raw HTML
- **MUST** allow only the link schemes `item:`, `https:`, `http:` and `mailto:`; show every other link as plain text
- **MUST NOT** load remote pictures; show a placeholder with the address
- **MUST** convert pasted HTML (and RTF through its HTML) to Markdown with the same rules, never store it as HTML (UX decision [D-62](item:46ec3446-e80d-538d-af6d-3c60b94c9e3d))
- **MUST** keep a collection of known attack strings that must render harmlessly, including pasted HTML
- **MUST NOT** rely on the Content Security Policy alone

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-052"   # attack strings render harmlessly
```

why: In a shared tree another person writes content; injected code could read every key on the device.

Source: [ADR-052-untrusted-content.md](item:f39760be-0139-5eba-ac69-bff9594a88dd)

title: ADR-073 Encryption hardening before release 1
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amends [ADR-015](item:0a4a5821-6c8b-5175-936c-4ba123adbdc3) (authenticated data), [ADR-012](item:33bd5096-18d5-5fa9-9dc1-c959db5793be) (extractable key), [ADR-028](item:510c155f-f2a3-5463-ac8d-0643a54f3e35) (key handed in for each operation) and [ADR-007](item:72d8232b-5c71-5140-9596-9e03184d4407) (exchange file header); owner decision 2026-11-15.

- **MUST** bind every plaintext envelope field except the nonce (the encryption's own input) and `ServerSequence` (envelope version, `KeyId`, `EventId`) plus the account id and a fixed context label as additional authenticated data
- **MUST** encrypt a payload wrapper object with room for optional parts (for example a later device signature), not the bare event
- **MUST** encrypt and decrypt only through a non-extractable key handle; **MUST** store the raw tree key only wrapped by a non-extractable device key, unwrapped only for pairing, sharing or key backup
- **MUST NOT** pass the raw tree key into .NET memory, logs or reports outside pairing, sharing or key backup
- **MUST** take production keys and nonces only from the browser's cryptographic random source; a test checks the production composition
- **MUST** encrypt snapshots, search index and drafts at rest with the tree key
- **MUST** keep the exchange file header to format version and `KeyId`, bound to the contents; account id, device labels and tree names go inside the encrypted part (the account id is also authenticated data of every envelope, taken from the tree access on both sides)
- **SHOULD** batch Web Crypto calls during replay

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-073"
```

why: Cheap now, impossible after release 1 freezes the formats; keeps doors open for signatures and an app lock.

Source: [ADR-073-encryption-hardening.md](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)

title: ADR-089 No user content in printed output
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

Proposed by an agent 2026-11-26 (clean-code review T9, option c), accepted by the owner 2026-11-26; amends no ADR.

- **MUST NOT** put user content into text that code prints: `ToString()`, exception messages, log and console output. User content is titles, notes and every other text the user typed, such as names of trees, tags, relation types and views, and device labels
- **MUST** override `ToString()` (or `PrintMembers`) on every record that holds user content, because the compiler-generated one prints every property
- **MAY** print ids, event types, kinds and counts, so local debugging stays possible; reports leave out ids as well ([ADR-051](item:70d87940-8c95-593a-ba9d-aa3fd8631e22))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-089"   # printed events, items and trees carry no titles or notes
```

why: Printed text leaves the device without the user choosing to share content (screenshots, browser consoles, bug reports, server logs), so end-to-end encryption ([ADR-015](item:0a4a5821-6c8b-5175-936c-4ba123adbdc3), [ADR-030](item:68a5428c-3b63-557c-b2c1-4957cf63343a)) must not leak through it.

Source: [ADR-089-no-content-in-printed-output.md](item:3ea75a26-012d-583d-9a57-97dfdb357ffa)

title: Outline features
note: Conflicts, relations, tags, undo, themes, views, focus, inbox, templates, headings

title: ADR-018 Conflicts are visible and resolved by the user
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7) (`relation.note-changed` carries `replaces`; relation notes are a kind of conflict), [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6) (`relation.type-changed` carries `replaces`) and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (`relation-type.set` replaces `relation-type.defined` and `display-name.set` in the list; display names leave the kinds of conflicts); owner decisions 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** let exactly these events name the changes they replace (`replaces`): `item.title-changed`, `item.note-changed`, `item.moved`, `relation-type.defined`, `display-name.set`, `tree.feature-changed`, `tree.server-changed`, `view.set` (amended by [ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7), [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): `relation.note-changed`, `relation.type-changed` and `relation-type.set` are in the list; `relation-type.defined` and `display-name.set` are not events of the format)
- **MUST NOT** treat concurrent changes with the same value as a conflict
- **MUST** list all kinds of conflicts (items, relation types, display names, tree features, server address, views) in the Conflict View (amended by [ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7), [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): relation notes and a relation's type are kinds of conflicts; display names are not)
- **MUST** let `item.deleted` carry `seen`, the highest clock received per device
- **MUST** derive conflicts from the log; MUST NOT store them
- **MUST** resolve a conflict by an ordinary event that replaces all competing changes

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-018"
```

why: Last-writer-wins can still pick the wrong value; the user sees and fixes it.

Source: [ADR-018-visible-conflicts.md](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d)

title: ADR-024 Relations separate from the tree
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

Amended by [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6) (a relation has its own id); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** model relations with `relation.added` / `relation.removed`, identified by from item, type id and to item (amended by [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6): identified by `relationId`; relations with equal from item, type and to item are shown as one)
- **MUST NOT** let relations change where an item sits
- **MUST NOT** connect trees: relations only point to items of the same tree; an `item:` text link whose target is in another tree (for example after copy and paste, [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e)) stays as text and is shown as not found, never as a working link
- **MUST** store the item ids of symmetric relations in a fixed order
- **MUST** hide relations of deleted items and show them again on restore

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-024"
```

why: Any number of typed connections without touching the single-parent tree.

Source: [ADR-024-relations.md](item:ffd6a5a2-d9ad-5537-ba6f-456f67d962b2)

title: ADR-025 Relation types defined per tree, predefined set
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** reference relation types by id, never by name
- **MUST** define types per tree by `relation-type.defined`; write the predefined set as events when a tree is created, with fixed ids
- **MUST NOT** build relation types into the app

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-025"
```

why: One mechanism for all types; the user owns every type; fixed ids avoid duplicates on merge.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that a small predefined set of relation types gives a good start, and that people adapt it rather than starting from nothing.

- **Outcome:** Relations are usable right away without inventing types first; everything stays changeable, because predefined types are ordinary events.
- **Assumption:** The starting set (related, supports, contradicts, example_of, cites, depends_on) fits how most people think; users rename, remove or add types when it doesn't fit, rather than giving up on relations.
- **Signal:** Feedback about relation types; answers to "Do the predefined relation types fit how you think?" (yes / partly / no); in the usage summary, without names: uses per predefined type, number of own types, number of renamed or removed predefined types.
- **Review when:** one predefined type is almost never used, or removed by most who answer · most users create own types that mean the same thing · relations are hardly used at all.
- **Superseded** by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (owner decision 2026-11-19): relation types are items and a new tree starts with only `related`; this card is kept as history and its signals are no longer collected.

Source: [ADR-025-predefined-relation-types.md](item:17b19d42-fcfc-57b1-b5aa-da9f2de567bd)

title: ADR-026 Translatable display names for structural elements
note:
