applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** give user-definable structural elements their names only through `display-name.set` / `display-name.removed`, per language
- **MUST** show display names in this order: device language, its base language, app resource files (predefined elements), any display name
- **MUST NOT** translate content (titles, notes) in the log
- **MUST NOT** translate content on the fly either: it would need an AI model reading the user's thoughts ([ADR-071](item:1bc7e63d-dcfc-5adb-87b2-dc10128daf48))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-026"
```

why: One translation mechanism for all structural elements; content stays as written.

Source: [ADR-026-translatable-display-names.md](item:7a9c0941-12b2-56b3-bd38-35768c06e193)

title: ADR-058 Tags as tree elements, typed with `@@`
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** define tags per tree as structural elements with an id (`tag.defined`), named only by `display-name.set` / `display-name.removed` ([ADR-026](item:7a9c0941-12b2-56b3-bd38-35768c06e193))
- **MUST** assign tags to items with `item.tagged` / `item.untagged`, identified by item id and tag id; adding the same tag twice yields one assignment; concurrent adding and removing is decided by the agreed event order, without conflict marking
- **MUST NOT** keep tags in an item's title or note; `@@name` typed in a title is an input shortcut that the application layer turns into an assignment when editing ends, matching an existing tag by its display name with the search matching rules, or defining a new tag
- **MUST** hide the tags of deleted items and show them again on restore
- **MUST** offer the same assignment without typing (tag picker when focused on the item), as the accessible alternative ([ADR-033](item:75be0950-c5ca-5362-8542-42881e719183))
- **MUST** make tags a tree feature (`tree.feature-changed`), switched on by default
- **MUST NOT** connect trees: a tag belongs to one tree
- **MUST** offer to join tags with the same display name (for example defined offline on two devices) by a `tag.joined` event (from tag, into tag); assignments of the joined tag then count for the target tag; the app never joins tags without asking

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-058"
```

why: Tags give items further dimensions besides the tree (UX decision [D-14](item:b34aea28-04c0-58d3-bf0d-d61fd3e436b6)); one mechanism with relations and display names keep renaming, translation and merging consistent.

Source: [ADR-058-tags.md](item:0453bf80-1508-5c0e-b3ce-6c43a5effc6b)

title: ADR-059 Undo writes new events; quick undo covers the user's own actions on this device
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e) (quick undo and the history skip export events, which record a fact, not a change); owner decisions 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18.

- **MUST** undo a change by writing ordinary new events that restore the previous state (for a delete: the restore of [ADR-005](item:84511883-937f-5636-b827-bee45d72fa11)); **MUST NOT** remove or alter events in the log
- **MUST** let every change be reverted from the item's history, whichever device or user made it
- **MUST** let quick undo (undo button, Ctrl+Z) step back only through the actions of the user on this device, in one sequence across all views, never through changes that arrived from other devices or users
- **MUST** derive the quick undo sequence from the log: this device's own events, newest first, skipping events already reverted; **MUST NOT** keep a separate undo list
- **MUST** let an undo event name the event it reverts (`reverts`, like git's "This reverts commit …"), so the history can show it and quick undo can skip reverted events
- **MUST** show what an undo reverses: bring the affected item into view and highlight it, or name the change with a way to go there; announce it through the live region ([ADR-033](item:75be0950-c5ca-5362-8542-42881e719183))
- **MUST** offer the usual text undo and redo within a draft while text is being edited, and turn the whole text change into one step of quick undo when editing ends; **MUST NOT** offer redo for other actions
- **MUST NOT** overwrite a later change from another device or user by quick undo: when the item was changed since, quick undo stops, names the later change and offers the item's history
- **MUST NOT** limit how far back quick undo reaches
- **MUST** decide undo in the application layer ([ADR-041](item:a9c65ed8-fe3b-5b54-948c-c92201d8d164)), so every component behaves the same

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-059"   # includes INV-14
```

why: The log is never rewritten, so undo is a revert like in git; limiting quick undo to the user's own actions keeps it predictable while sync brings in other changes (UX decision [D-25](item:4b49ca2d-8883-5097-8626-ab3999cd72c2)).

Source: [ADR-059-undo.md](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)

title: ADR-060 Themes of trees and branches are shared through events
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** record the theme of a tree or of an item by an event (`theme.set` with the target tree or item and a theme id), so all devices and all users of a tree show the same theme; themes are always available, not a tree feature
- **MUST** decide concurrent `theme.set` events for the same target silently by the agreed event order (last writer wins), without `replaces` and without a conflict; the history shows both changes
- **MUST** let an item's theme apply to its whole branch, shown for all its children unless a child sets its own; otherwise the tree's theme applies
- **MUST** ship at least the themes "Paper" (default) and "Inbox" (starting theme of every inbox, [ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c))
- **MUST** reference themes by fixed ids shipped with the app; **MUST** fall back to the default theme for an unknown theme id (tested in the format tests: an older app shows the default theme for a newer theme id)
- **MUST** build every component from semantic design tokens, so a theme only swaps token values (palette, font, density, note preview); **MUST** meet the contrast rules ([ADR-033](item:75be0950-c5ca-5362-8542-42881e719183)) in every theme, also for a tinted branch inside another theme
- **MUST NOT** treat themes as device state ([ADR-013](item:2503cff6-630e-5fbd-89f6-22dd074fee11)): the theme belongs to the content, like a tree's name

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-060"
```

why: The owner chooses a theme to support the mood of a project; it has to look the same on every device and for everyone who shares the tree (UX decisions [D-34](item:cd0c6b92-ccc2-539a-9123-bcb1de7ee943) to [D-36](item:5430cc3b-6ce6-5bee-a99b-0f17a66f36fa)).

Source: [ADR-060-shared-themes.md](item:bf684b01-1e00-5613-b339-982fb1ed2313)

title: ADR-062 Views belong to items
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** let every item, and the tree itself, carry an ordered list of views; without one, the item has only the outline view
- **MUST** define a view by events (`view.set` with the owner (an item or the tree), a view id, its name, its query, its layout and `replaces`; `view.removed`), so views are shared like content
- **MUST** keep every older query readable by every later version (secured by the format tests)
- **MUST** store the query as structured data with its own format version (words, tags, "changed recently", later filters), never as code; the scope is the owner's branch, or the whole tree for views of the tree
- **MUST** reference layouts by fixed ids shipped with the app (outline now; board, columns and others later); **MUST** fall back to the outline for an unknown layout
- **MUST** compute the results on the device from the projection and the search index; **MUST NOT** store results in the log
- **MUST** offer at the tree level a view that lists all views of the tree, with the path of their items
- **MUST** hide the views of a deleted item and show them again on restore
- **MUST** let concurrent changes of the same view follow [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d) (last writer wins, conflict listed); `view.set` is one of the events that carry `replaces`
- **MUST** treat a view's name as content written by the user, not as a translatable display name
- **MUST** keep views always available, not a tree feature

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-062"
```

why: A project carries its own perspectives (saved searches now, layouts later) like its theme, without extra items in the tree (UX decisions [D-38](item:38321d20-aa15-5504-9066-4be7bbb3d8e0), [D-39](item:2f9a2ce2-ed4c-5e0a-8d34-a9eca53f49f3)).

Source: [ADR-062-views-on-items.md](item:3ecc302d-7862-5524-8174-9dff17cce88a)

title: ADR-065 "Focus" instead of "Zoom"
note:
applies_to: `docs/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `tests/**`

- **MUST** call making an item the temporary top of the view, showing its branch and the item as a page (title, tags, note; [ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)), **Focus** in documents, code, tests, the test id catalogue and the app's wording; **MUST NOT** call it "zoom"
- **MUST** keep "zoom" only for magnifying (pinch or browser zoom), which the app does not redefine

verify:

```bash
grep -rniE '\bzoom(ed|ing)?\b' docs/architecture.md docs/adr src tests | grep -v ADR-065 | grep -v 'magnifying' | wc -l   # expect 0
```

why: "Zoom" suggests magnifying; the owner means concentrating on one item and its branch (UX decisions [D-56](item:5161c8a5-edfe-5ed9-8747-64b1b9878d7e), [D-57](item:0b14f20b-fccf-5776-a31d-86c9d71d3b0a)).

Source: [ADR-065-focus.md](item:37387329-c750-5cd5-9367-9f45ee092e98)

title: ADR-066 The inbox is a marked item, always last
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253) and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (the tree name also skips the Tags and Relation types branches); owner decision 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** create the inbox as an ordinary item when a tree is created and mark it with `tree.inbox-set`
- **MUST** give a new inbox the predefined theme "Inbox" (fixed id) by an ordinary `theme.set`, changeable like any theme
- **MUST** create captured thoughts inside the inbox
- **MUST** show the inbox last at the top level, whatever its stored position; "top level, last" places items before it
- **MUST** let the inbox expand, be focused, themed and tagged like any branch; **MUST NOT** let it be moved or deleted
- **MUST** skip the inbox when taking the tree name from the first visible top-level item (amended by [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): also the Tags and Relation types branches)
- **MUST** let the latest `tree.inbox-set` in the agreed order win; after importing a tree into another, the importing device writes `tree.inbox-set` for the target's own inbox, the other inbox becomes an ordinary item, and the app offers to move its contents
- **MUST** offer the inbox's full item menu from the global menu (More › Inbox)

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-066"
```

why: An inbox that behaves like a branch can be expanded and sorted by drag and drop; last at the top level keeps the tree's own content first (prototype feedback, UX decisions [D-1](item:f92ffb50-b86e-5f60-bc95-933beca12283), [D-5](item:a32e82dc-aeea-5131-b535-ecdecad75a4c)).

Source: [ADR-066-inbox.md](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c)

title: ADR-067 One action, one undo step
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

- **MUST** let every event carry an action id (`actionId`) that is shared by all events written for one user action (for example a bulk move of several items, pasting indented text as several items, duplicating a branch, a template); a single-event action gets its own action id
- **MUST** let quick undo ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)) revert all events of the most recent action of this device together, as one step, with one undo event per reverted event (each naming it in `reverts`)
- **MUST** show and announce the undone action as one change (for example "Undone: moved 7 items to 'Ideas'"), following [ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)'s rule that undo shows what it reverts
- **MUST** treat an action as stopped by [ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)'s rule as a whole: if any of its items was changed since by another device or user, quick undo stops and offers the history
- **MUST** add `actionId` to the event format before the first release, so no stored event lacks it

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-067"
```

why: Bulk actions on touch (multi-select, paste as items) write many events at once; undoing them one by one would take as many taps as items (open question 14 of the UX concept and the outliner comparison); the field is cheap now and hard to add once events are stored.

Source: [ADR-067-one-action-one-undo-step.md](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)

title: ADR-068 Templates are marked items, valid below their parent
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** keep a template as an ordinary item with its branch, marked by events (`item.template-set` / `item.template-removed` with the item id), so templates sync, are shared and keep their history like any content
- **MUST** make a template valid in the branch of its parent; a template at the top level is valid in the whole tree; moving the template item changes where it is valid; no special root item exists for this
- **MUST** create an item from a template by copying the template's branch as one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)): new ids, the template marking not copied
- **MUST** rewrite `item:` links and relations between items of the template's branch to the copies; links and relations pointing outside the branch are kept as they are
- **MUST** recognise `::` as the template shortcut only at the start of an empty line; `\::` there keeps two literal colons
- **MUST NOT** store a reference from a created item to its template; a template's tags are copied with its branch, so items made from it can be found by tag (UX decision [D-112](item:7a7aaf2c-387f-5785-8175-0b967306a5bb))
- **MUST NOT** write templates into new trees; the tutorial tree carries a set of templates (Person, Talk or meeting, Source, Decision, Idea) that the user copies into their own trees ([ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e))
- **MUST** leave templates out of search, "Changed recently", counts and the Markdown and OPML export, unless the user asks for templates; the JSON export ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)) always contains them
- **MUST NOT** store the display-only group row ("Templates · n") that the outline shows for the templates of a branch; it is a rendering of the marked items

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-068"
```

why: Templates as items need no second structure next to the tree and are edited and moved with the tools the user already knows; "valid below the parent" gives branch templates and tree-wide templates without a root item (UX decisions [D-107](item:4f4d3d60-a8be-57e4-88e4-a02b681d1762), [D-108](item:d381932f-aec9-52bb-8749-a3207b727941), [D-110](item:38ee2a5e-3f31-531b-b8f8-c37d25d98b49)).

Source: [ADR-068-templates.md](item:10565c29-e7be-5e3f-bfaa-6249e2241cab)

title: ADR-072 A heading is a thought; Focus shows a thought as a page
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2) ("Headings become thoughts" is a tree feature, on by default); owner decision 2026-11-17.

Proposed by the UX concept (decisions [D-151](item:768c4ff2-e921-5d89-9ef9-d0eed2cd469a), [D-153](item:539925b0-f7b5-542f-babc-d3ba4299da64), [D-155](item:04fbcfd6-9f88-5c63-9285-73811e1a7c7b)). Touches section 8 (text: "notes are Markdown without headings") and [ADR-065](item:37387329-c750-5cd5-9367-9f45ee092e98) (Focus).

- **MUST** show, when focused on an item, its title, tags, note and its branch on one page; there is no separate detail page
- **MUST** treat a heading entered in a note as a new item: on confirming the heading line, create an item inside the focused item (first position), with the heading text as its title and the text that followed the heading as its note, as one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)); only existing events are used (`item.created`, `item.note-changed`)
- **MUST NOT** store Markdown headings in notes written in the app; all other Markdown of notes stays as it is (amended by [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2): only while the tree feature is on)
- **MUST** ask before converting when text containing headings is pasted or imported into a note: turn the headings into items (deeper headings become items inside them; text before the first heading stays the note), or keep one note with the heading lines kept as bold text
- **MUST** keep notes that already contain headings readable (events are immutable): they are rendered, and the user is offered the same conversion
- **SHOULD** write items as headings in the readable Markdown export and read headings as items in the readable import ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)), so a document and its tree round-trip
- **MUST** write levels deeper than Markdown's six heading levels as nested lists in the readable export, and read them back as items, so deep branches round-trip too

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-072"
```

why: The structure of a text is the tree. A thought that grows headings grows into a branch without a separate step, and the page reads like a document (the owner's model: Word's outline view).

Source: [ADR-072-headings-are-thoughts.md](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)

title: ADR-077 A note on a relation
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6) (the note is keyed by the relation's id) and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (relation types are items); owner decisions 2026-11-19.

Amends [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d) (adds `relation.note-changed` to the events that carry `replaces`, and relation notes to the kinds of conflicts in the Conflict View); owner decision 2026-11-17 (Zettelkasten decision 3), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** store the note of a relation (why two items are connected) only in `relation.note-changed` with `fromItemId`, `typeId`, `toItemId`, `note`, `format`, `replaces` (amended by [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6): `relationId`, `note`, `format`, `replaces`); the full text in each event, one event per editing session
- **MUST NOT** put a note on `relation.added`, and **MUST NOT** use `item.note-changed` for it
- **MUST** key the note by the relation's three parts, with the item ids of symmetric types in the relation's fixed order ([ADR-024](item:ffd6a5a2-d9ad-5537-ba6f-456f67d962b2)); an empty note removes it (amended by [ADR-083](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6): keyed by the relation's id)
- **MUST** hide the note while its relation is removed, its type removed (amended by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): its type item deleted or outside the Relation types branch) or one of its items deleted, and show it again when the relation comes back
- **MUST** treat concurrent changes of the same note as a visible conflict, resolved like item notes ([ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d)); undo writes a new event naming the one it reverts ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0))
- **MUST** apply the text rules of item notes: Markdown without headings ([ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)), normalised ([ADR-029](item:60a30705-4e16-547f-9365-4d928fe34dc1)), rendered as untrusted content ([ADR-052](item:f39760be-0139-5eba-ac69-bff9594a88dd)), found by the on-device search
- **MUST** carry relation notes in the readable JSON export and import ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)); their Markdown form is fixed with the Zettelkasten export ([zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-077"
```

why: The reason for a connection is often the actual thought (Zettelkasten practice: "builds on X because …"); a separate event built like item notes keeps conflicts, undo, history and older apps (which skip unknown events, [ADR-016](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3)) working without a special case.

Source: [ADR-077-relation-notes.md](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7)

title: ADR-079 Headings become thoughts is a tree feature
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amends [ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3) (headings in notes), [ADR-029](item:60a30705-4e16-547f-9365-4d928fe34dc1) (notes without headings) and [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) (reading headings as items on import); owner decision 2026-11-17 (Zettelkasten session), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** make "Headings become thoughts" a tree feature (`tree.feature-changed`), switched on by default, so all devices and users of a tree write the same way
- **MUST**, while it is on, behave as [ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3) says, except that "Keep as one note" when pasting or importing keeps the headings as headings instead of bold lines
- **MUST**, while it is off, keep headings typed, pasted or imported in the note, without asking, and store them with `format: markdown`
- **MUST** keep "Turn headings into thoughts" ([D-153](item:539925b0-f7b5-542f-babc-d3ba4299da64)) available for a single item's note whatever the feature's state
- **MUST NOT** change the projection or any stored event when the feature changes; it only changes what the editor and the import do (section 9, tree features)
- **SHOULD** offer to switch the feature off when an Obsidian vault is imported as a new tree
- **MUST** keep relation notes without headings ([ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-079"
```

why: Zettelkasten notes often keep their headings (and `[[note#heading]]` links point at them); forcing them into thoughts or bold lines would break the round trip with Obsidian. The shape of a tree's content belongs to the tree, so the choice is shared, not per device.

Source: [ADR-079-keep-headings-tree-feature.md](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2)

title: ADR-081 One name per structural element, no translation inside the tree
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amends [ADR-026](item:7a9c0941-12b2-56b3-bd38-35768c06e193) (display names per language) and the translation part of [ADR-058](item:0453bf80-1508-5c0e-b3ce-6c43a5effc6b)'s reason; owner decision 2026-11-18 (Zettelkasten session), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19. Settles the format before release 1, while nothing is stored.

- **MUST** give a user-definable structural element (relation type, tag) one name per field (`name`, `reverseName`), set by `display-name.set` / `display-name.removed` without a `language` field
- **MUST** show the name stored in the tree; for a predefined element without a stored name, the name from the app's resource files in the device's language
- **MUST NOT** store names of one element in several languages, and **MUST NOT** translate names or content ([ADR-071](item:1bc7e63d-dcfc-5adb-87b2-dc10128daf48))
- **MUST** write no stored name when a tree is created, so predefined elements follow the device's language until the user renames them

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-081"
```

why: A name in the user's own words is what the user typed; per-language names add UI, conflicts and import/export cases for a rare need (co-authors of different languages), while predefined names still follow the device's language through the app's resources.

Source: [ADR-081-one-name-no-translation.md](item:a7e0865f-c126-5137-8291-7544b44ca713)

title: ADR-082 Tags are items in the tree's Tags branch
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Supersedes [ADR-058](item:0453bf80-1508-5c0e-b3ce-6c43a5effc6b) (keeps its `@@` shortcut, picker, tree feature, one-tree and join rules) and amends [ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c) (the tree name also skips the Tags branch), [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e) (tags matched by title) and [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) (tags imported as items); owner decisions 2026-11-19 (session "Tags and relation types as items", decisions 2 and 5), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19. Settles the format before release 1, while stored formats are still free to change ([ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a)).

- **MUST** create a branch "Tags" as an ordinary item when a tree is created and mark it with `tree.tags-set` (`itemId`); its title is written in the app language chosen on the creating device; the latest `tree.tags-set` in the agreed order wins, as for the inbox ([ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c)); **MUST NOT** let the Tags branch be moved or deleted; **MUST** skip it when taking the tree name ([ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c))
- **MUST** treat every item inside the Tags branch as a tag, by its place, with no mark event: its title is the tag's name, its note the tag's description, its child items its nested tags
- **MUST** assign tags with `item.tagged` / `item.untagged` (`itemId`, `tagId`), where `tagId` is the tag item's id; adding the same tag twice yields one assignment; concurrent adding and removing is decided by the agreed event order, without conflict marking
- **MUST** hide the assignments of a tag while its item is deleted or outside the Tags branch, and show them again when it is restored or moved back; **MUST** hide the tags of deleted items and show them again on restore
- **MUST** let a parent tag include its nested tags when filtering, searching and counting; a chip shows only the tag that was assigned
- **MUST NOT** keep tags in an item's title or note; `@@name` typed in a title is an input shortcut that the application layer turns into an assignment when editing ends, matching a tag by its title with the search matching rules, or creating a new tag item in the Tags branch
- **MUST** offer the same assignment without typing (tag picker), as the accessible alternative ([ADR-033](item:75be0950-c5ca-5362-8542-42881e719183))
- **MUST** offer to join tags with the same title (for example made offline on two devices) as one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)): `tag.joined` (`fromTagId`, `intoTagId`), the joined tag's children moved under the target, its note appended to the target's note below a separator line, the joined tag item deleted; assignments of the joined tag count for the target while the `tag.joined` holds, although the joined item is deleted; undoing the join ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)) restores the item and its own assignments; the app never joins tags without asking
- **MUST** make tags a tree feature (`tree.feature-changed`), switched on by default; off hides chips, `@@`, the picker and the Tags branch (outline, navigation, search) and keeps all assignments
- **MUST NOT** connect trees: a tag belongs to one tree; copy and paste matches tags by title ([ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e))
- **MUST**, when importing a tree, a JSON export or an Obsidian vault as a copy, move its tag items into the target's Tags branch in the same action as the imported content, without matching, and then offer to join tags with equal titles; when importing a tree, the importing device writes `tree.tags-set` for the target's own branch in the same action, and the imported tree's former branch becomes an ordinary item (as [ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c) does for the inbox); an update import ([ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e)) matches tag items by their `thoughttree` id
- **MUST** export tags to Obsidian as `tags:` with nested tags as paths (`a/b`), and import nested tags `#a/b` as nested tag items; **MAY** offer to import folder names as nested tag items when folders do not build the tree, whether and by default is decided in the import-flow sketch (owner decision 2026-11-19); each tag is also written as a note in the folder of the Tags branch, carrying its description and its id ([zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-082"
```

why: A tag that is an item gets a description, nesting, a place for navigation ([D-150](item:4c64f9a0-5366-5c75-a5b5-78dafa145f02)) and history without a second mechanism; its place in a marked branch makes it a tag, as the inbox is marked (owner's drivers: folders as tags, navigable tags, a tag with a description, nested tags).

Source: [ADR-082-tags-are-items.md](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253)

title: ADR-083 Relations have an id
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amends [ADR-024](item:ffd6a5a2-d9ad-5537-ba6f-456f67d962b2) (identity by from item, type and to item), [ADR-077](item:b8470a09-0a1d-557c-97cf-a2370565e1d7) (the note is keyed by the relation's id) and [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d) (adds `relation.type-changed` to the events that carry `replaces`); owner decision 2026-11-19 (session "Tags and relation types as items", decision 3a), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19. Settles the format before release 1, while stored formats are still free to change ([ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a)): an id cannot be added cleanly to relations stored by release 1.

- **MUST** give every relation an id from the replaceable id generator ([ADR-034](item:5ce571c4-8e3f-5da8-8f84-cd3dade367d6)): `relation.added` (`relationId`, `fromItemId`, `typeId`, `toItemId`)
- **MUST** change a relation's type only by `relation.type-changed` (`relationId`, `typeId`, `replaces`); concurrent changes of the type are a visible conflict ([ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d))
- **MUST** remove and restore a relation by `relation.removed` / `relation.restored` (`relationId`); undo restores the same relation ([ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0)); concurrent removing and restoring of the same relation is decided by the agreed event order, without conflict marking (owner decision 2026-11-19); removing a relation shown as one (see below) removes every relation id it stands for, in one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a))
- **MUST** key the note of a relation by its id: `relation.note-changed` (`relationId`, `note`, `format`, `replaces`), so the note and its history stay when the type changes
- **MUST** show relations with equal from item, type and to item (for symmetric types in either order) as one; if more than one of them carries a note, the notes are shown as a visible conflict
- **MUST NOT** make relations items: a relation has no place in the tree ([ADR-023](item:4da40799-3f96-5b48-b124-3848e7ed2711), [ADR-024](item:ffd6a5a2-d9ad-5537-ba6f-456f67d962b2))
- **MUST** give copies new relation ids when copying, pasting or creating from a template ([ADR-068](item:10565c29-e7be-5e3f-bfaa-6249e2241cab), [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e)); the Obsidian files carry no relation ids, so the update import ([ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e)) matches relations by from item, type and to item

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-083"
```

why: A reassignable type with its note and history needs an identity apart from the type; duplicates made offline are rare and are shown as one.

Source: [ADR-083-relation-ids.md](item:d79b27f0-fbc8-58df-bf6c-8d80502733b6)

title: ADR-084 Relation types are items; a new tree has only `related`
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Supersedes [ADR-025](item:17b19d42-fcfc-57b1-b5aa-da9f2de567bd) (with its bet card), [ADR-026](item:7a9c0941-12b2-56b3-bd38-35768c06e193) and [ADR-081](item:a7e0865f-c126-5137-8291-7544b44ca713), and amends [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d) (`relation-type.set` replaces `relation-type.defined` and `display-name.set` among the events that carry `replaces`; display names leave the conflict kinds), [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) (no type is reused by a fixed id; no display names), [ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c) (the tree name also skips the Relation types branch) and [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e) (types matched by title); the [ADR-025](item:17b19d42-fcfc-57b1-b5aa-da9f2de567bd) bet card is retired (bets.md); owner decisions 2026-11-19 (session "Tags and relation types as items", decisions 3, 4 and 5), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19. Settles the format before release 1, while stored formats are still free to change ([ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a)).

- **MUST** create a branch "Relation types" as an ordinary item when a tree is created and mark it with `tree.relation-types-set` (`itemId`); the latest marking in the agreed order wins; **MUST NOT** let the branch be moved or deleted; **MUST** skip it when taking the tree name ([ADR-066](item:d47b0df5-b7f2-5735-83eb-8681e57b5f6c))
- **MUST** treat every item inside that branch as a relation type, by its place: its title is the type's name, its note says what the type means; `relation-type.set` (`itemId`, `symmetric`, `reverseName`, `replaces`) keeps whether the type is symmetric and its reverse name; a type item without it is directed and has no reverse name
- **MUST** reference a type by its item id, never by its name; **MUST** hide the relations of a type while its item is deleted or outside the branch, and show them again when it comes back
- **MUST** create in a new tree exactly one type, `related` (symmetric), as an ordinary type item with a new id, and mark it as the tree's default relation type by `tree.default-relation-type-set` (`itemId`); a new relation gets the default type ([D-13](item:9e6c7dfe-2e60-59be-9006-9af6309a5f11)); the latest marking in the agreed order wins; when importing a tree, the importing device writes the marking for the target's default in the same action; the user can make another type the default; **MUST NOT** give any item a fixed id
- **MUST NOT** build other relation types into the app or into new trees; the tutorial offers further types as ordinary items to copy (new ids, matched by title, [ADR-069](item:0f689d96-0e7b-5a8f-8499-5c103bd49e5e)); duplicate types after an import are allowed; an import as a copy moves the imported type items into the target's Relation types branch in the same action, without matching, `related` included; when importing a tree, the importing device writes `tree.relation-types-set` for the target's own branch in the same action, and the imported tree's former branch becomes an ordinary item; an update import ([ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e)) matches type items by their `thoughttree` id
- **MUST** write the titles of the items made at tree creation ("Tags", "Relation types", "related", the inbox) in the app language chosen on the creating device; they are content like any title and are never translated by the app
- **MUST NOT** use display names: no structural element with a name of its own is left (`display-name.set` / `display-name.removed` are not events of the format)
- **MUST** export every type to Obsidian by its title, `related` included, and also as a note in the folder of the Relation types branch with its meaning, its id, `thoughttree-symmetric` and `thoughttree-reverse`; on import a type key resolves to the type note by its id when the files carry one, else by title, defining a new type item for an unknown key ([zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md))
- **MUST** make relations a tree feature (`tree.feature-changed`), switched on by default; off hides relations, the map's relations and the Relation types branch, and keeps them

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-084"
```

why: A type that is an item gets a note saying what it means, history and copying by copy and paste, with the same mechanism as tags; one predefined type keeps [D-13](item:9e6c7dfe-2e60-59be-9006-9af6309a5f11) without filling new trees, and names written as content need no translation mechanism.

Source: [ADR-084-relation-types-are-items.md](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2)

title: Export and import
note: Readable export and import of trees and branches

title: ADR-019 Unencrypted export only as readable tree
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amended by [ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e) (new ids only for items the tree does not know; update import), [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2) (reading headings as items is a tree feature), [ADR-080](item:5512e2ce-cc4b-5c03-9cca-340487536507) (a branch, not only the whole tree), [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253) (tags imported as items) and [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2) (no type is reused by a fixed id; no display names); owner decisions 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** export unencrypted only the current tree (Markdown, OPML, JSON), without history, deleted items or device information (amended by [ADR-080](item:5512e2ce-cc4b-5c03-9cca-340487536507): also one branch)
- **MUST NOT** export the event log unencrypted
- **MUST NOT** make readable export a default or automatic; MUST require a confirmed warning and mark the file name as unencrypted
- **MUST** import readable files as a new tree or into an item, with ordinary events of the current event types (for example `item.created`, and for JSON also relations, relation types, display names, tags, themes, views, template markings and note changes) (amended by [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253), [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): tags and relation types are items in the marked branches; display names do not exist)
- **SHOULD** write items as headings in the Markdown export and read headings as items ([ADR-072](item:62d06ce7-f9af-581e-9fad-86105c54e5a3)) (amended by [ADR-079](item:89a6dcae-9f47-5920-907f-e286526addb2): reading headings as items is a tree feature)
- **MUST** give every imported item a new id and rewrite `item:` links within the imported content; reuse predefined relation types by their fixed ids (amended by [ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e): only items the tree does not know get new ids, an update import matches by id; amended by [ADR-084](item:705c6e4b-83f7-5842-beb8-170c019a04e2): no item has a fixed id, imported type items move into the target's Relation types branch)

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-019"
```

why: A backup without the key and a way in and out of ThoughtTree; history stays protected.

Source: [ADR-019-readable-export.md](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)

title: ADR-078 Re-importing a readable export updates the tree it came from
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

Amends [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) (new ids only for items the tree does not know) and [ADR-059](item:23cd8632-6a91-51e3-9452-e5d6907a66d0) (quick undo and the history skip export events, which record a fact, not a change); owner decisions 2026-11-17 (Zettelkasten decision 4b) and 2026-11-18 (export events), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** write into every readable export the id of each item (Obsidian form: a `thoughttree` property in each file's frontmatter; JSON: the item id; the one-document Markdown and OPML forms carry no ids and always import as a copy) and once per export the id of its export event
- **MUST** write, for every readable export, an export event into the log: `item.exported` (`itemId`, `form`, `format`, `seen`) when exported from an item's actions, `tree.exported` (`form`, `format`, `seen`) for the whole tree; `seen` is the export point (the highest clock received per device, as on `item.deleted`), `form` is folders or flat files with an `up` property
- **MUST NOT** put device information into the exported files ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)): the export point stays in the encrypted log, the files carry only the export event's id
- **MUST NOT** undo an export event with undo; it records a fact, takes part in no conflict and is shown in the history of its item or tree
- **MUST** preselect the form of the latest export event of the same item or tree for the next export
- **MUST** offer, when readable files carry ids of items of the tree they are imported into, "Update from these files" besides importing a copy
- **MUST**, on update, write ordinary events for known items (title, note, move, tags, relations, relation notes), and create items with new ids only for content without a known id ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983))
- **MUST** let each update event replace only the changes known at the export point, so a change made in the app after the export becomes a visible conflict ([ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d)), never an overwrite; when the export event has not reached this device (or the files carry none), an update replaces nothing known, and the app suggests exchanging with the exporting device first
- **MUST** add or remove tags and relations only by the difference between the file and the state at the export point, so connections made in the app after the export stay
- **MUST NOT** delete items whose files are missing; list them in the import report and delete them only after the user confirms
- **MUST** write the whole update as one action ([ADR-067](item:d2013d4a-3ba0-5b14-807c-042d942e7b6a)), undone in one step
- **MUST** read the export's form from its export event, without asking again
- **MUST** import a vault that carries no ids as a copy; notes are not matched by file path or foreign properties

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-078"
```

why: A round trip through other tools (Obsidian) must update the thoughts it came from without duplicates and without losing changes made meanwhile; the existing conflict mechanism does the safety work. Export events keep device information out of the unencrypted files; in a shared tree co-authors can see that and when someone exported (owner decision 2026-11-18).

Source: [ADR-078-update-import.md](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e)

title: ADR-080 Readable export and import of a branch, where the user is
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Contracts/**`

Amends [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) (a branch, not only the whole tree); owner decision 2026-11-17 (Zettelkasten session), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MUST** offer readable export of an item with its whole branch from the item's actions (its ⋯ menu and Focus), in every readable format, the Obsidian form included
- **MUST** write a single item without children as one `.md` file, and a branch as a zip of files
- **MUST** keep every rule of [ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983) for a branch: unencrypted only after a confirmed warning, never automatic, no history, deleted items or device information, file name marked as unencrypted
- **MUST** offer "Import into this thought…" in the same place, accepting one or several files or a zip; files carrying ids of this tree update their items ([ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e))
- **MUST** write links to items outside the exported branch so that Obsidian can resolve them against earlier exports (the form is fixed with the Zettelkasten export, [zettelkasten-claim.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/zettelkasten-claim.md))

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-080"
```

why: A user who remembers "I want this in Obsidian too" exports it where they are, without exporting the whole tree; a branch reveals less than the tree.

title: Client and UI
note: Blazor client, texts, accessibility, updates, switches, fonts and how UI work follows the UX concept

title: ADR-001 Client in Blazor WebAssembly
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** build the client in C# with Blazor WebAssembly, delivered as a PWA
- **MUST NOT** add a JavaScript UI framework (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, …)
- **SHOULD** limit JavaScript interop to browser APIs without .NET equivalent (IndexedDB, Web Crypto, service worker, file and share APIs)

verify:

```bash
grep -rlE '"(react|vue|@angular/core|svelte)"' --include=package.json src | wc -l   # expect 0
```

why: The developer works in C#; one language across client and server.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that one language for everything is worth Blazor's cost in download size and speed on phones.

- **Outcome:** One person with agents builds client and server in C#, shares Domain and Contracts without duplication, and works with one test harness.
- **Assumption:** Download size and speed are acceptable on phones, and one ecosystem outweighs JavaScript's richer UI libraries.
- **Signal:** Room left in the size budget; performance reports and feedback; answers to "Does ThoughtTree start fast enough on your phone?" (yes / sometimes slow / too slow).
- **Review when:** the size budget can't be kept · PF8 (app ready from the cache within 1.5 s) is missed on a mid-range phone once the client shell exists · several performance reports about start or input arrive · a key UI part (for example Markdown editing on the phone) is only available in good quality as a JavaScript library.
- **Reviewed 2026-11-25 (owner, spike 1 decision 5b):** the trigger "the storage and AOT spike misses the targets on a mid-range phone" was reached for PF1: the empty .NET app alone needs 1.25 to 1.74 s cold and 1.09 to 1.33 s from the cache on the phone (8 GB, Chrome and Firefox, AOT and interpreted); the snapshot adds about 0.5 s with AOT. Kept: the miss is below a second, not a multiple, and the alternative is a rewrite in JavaScript. PF1 now counts from app ready, app start is covered by PF8 and PF9; the spike trigger is replaced by the PF8 trigger above.

Source: [ADR-001-blazor-webassembly.md](item:b1e9b6bd-456d-5225-b054-3feb752f7206)

title: ADR-031 Kinds of switches
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Domain/**`

- **MUST** keep switches apart by kind: release flags, experiment flags, operations flags, permission flags, tree features, device settings
- **MUST** load release flags only from configuration shipped with the app; remove them once their feature is complete
- **MUST** assign experiment flags only per account on the server or by a local draw on the device; each experiment has a bet card and ends by its review
- **MUST** store permission flags and server-assigned experiment flags only as flags per account, and report them to the device during sync; **MUST** keep a locally drawn experiment flag as device state ([ADR-013](item:2503cff6-630e-5fbd-89f6-22dd074fee11)), never synced and never sent to the server
- **MUST NOT** use a third-party flag service, tracking or telemetry; **MUST NOT** write flags into events
- **MUST** record tree features by `tree.feature-changed`
- **MUST** let switches only hide commands and UI; the projection always applies every known event

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-031"
```

why: Switches serve development, experiments, operations and permissions without making trees differ or collecting data.

Source: [ADR-031-switches.md](item:534a3b01-e490-5e57-b9f5-1e7669de59d1)

title: ADR-032 App texts in resource files

applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** load culture data for all languages
- **MUST** keep Easy-language variants as their own sets of resource files (for example `de-x-easy`, `en-x-easy`), chosen in the settings like a language; the tutorial exists in Easy language from the start


title: ADR-033 Accessible, direction-neutral UI
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** aim for WCAG 2.2, level AA: meet every automatically checkable criterion, and treat the rest through specs, keyboard-only runs and user feedback
- **MUST** make every component usable with screen readers and keyboard only
- **MUST** offer an alternative (menu or keyboard command) for every drag or gesture
- **MUST** use CSS logical properties; MUST NOT use `left`/`right` for layout direction
- **MUST** render titles and note paragraphs with `dir="auto"`
- **MUST** give elements showing a domain concept a `data-testid` from the catalogue; controls are found by role and accessible name
- **MUST** announce changes that are not immediately visible through a live region
- **MUST** keep touch targets at least 24×24 CSS pixels

verify:

```bash
grep -rE '(margin|padding|border)-(left|right)|(^|[^-])(left|right):|float:|text-align: *(left|right)' --include=*.css --include=*.razor src/ThoughtTree.Client | wc -l   # expect 0
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-033"
```

why: Accessibility and a mirrored interface cannot be added later without reworking every component.

Source: [ADR-033-accessible-ui.md](item:75be0950-c5ca-5362-8542-42881e719183)

title: ADR-036 User-controlled app updates
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** check for and apply app updates only with the user's consent; exception: an installed PWA opened online lets the browser check for a new service worker by itself (about once a day), which the app cannot prevent; the app still applies updates only with consent
- **MUST** rebuild snapshots and search index after an update

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-036"
```

why: Update checks reveal the IP address; users in risky places must control them.

Source: [ADR-036-user-controlled-updates.md](item:7db9fef2-7ffe-5038-beb0-ca224f3a3da7)

title: ADR-041 Client application layer, thin components
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** put use cases, UI state and UI decisions into ThoughtTree.Client.App, plain C# without Razor or browser dependencies
- **MUST** keep Razor components to showing state and forwarding user input
- **MUST** keep navigation state (focus, selection, scroll position) per view, so several views can exist at once (structure sidebar, side-by-side panes)
- **MUST** enforce privacy-critical confirmations (sharing, unencrypted export, importing a tree into another) in the application layer, so no component can bypass them
- **MUST NOT** use HTML snapshot tests; assert meaning instead

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-041"
```

why: UI behaviour becomes fast, deterministic unit tests and runs in the simulation; thin components are hard to get wrong.

Source: [ADR-041-client-application-layer.md](item:a9c65ed8-fe3b-5b54-948c-c92201d8d164)

title: ADR-042 Browser APIs behind interfaces
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`

- **MUST** reach every browser API (local store, Web Crypto, file and share APIs, QR scanner, clipboard, service worker) only through a C# interface
- **MUST** keep JavaScript interop implementations thin, without logic
- **MUST** provide a fake implementation of every interface for tests
- **MUST NOT** call `IJSRuntime` outside the adapter implementations; adapters and UI share the Client project, so this is enforced by architecture tests per namespace, not by the banned API analyzer
- **MUST NOT** suppress analyzer or architecture rules (`#pragma warning disable`, `SuppressMessage`) outside an approved list of files, checked in CI

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-042"   # architecture tests: IJSRuntime only in the adapters namespace; no unapproved suppressions
```

why: Logic stays testable without a browser; the simulation needs every adapter faked.

Source: [ADR-042-browser-adapters.md](item:808d9792-d2f3-5a38-b0ef-6a0f94c3d6ae)

title: ADR-061 System font first, shipped fonts under the SIL Open Font License
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `**/*.csproj`, `**/package.json`

- **MUST** use the device's system font as the base font, so the first load downloads no font
- **MUST** ship every other font with the app from its own origin ([ADR-045](item:4ed194a5-683a-5f25-9867-341f6922bd57)); **MUST NOT** load fonts from third parties
- **MUST** download shipped fonts in the background after start and keep them for offline use; until a theme's font is available, show the system font
- **MUST** download a font only when a theme in use on this device needs it, not all shipped fonts at once
- **MAY** use fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (OFL); approves OFL for fonts as a "similar permissive licence" of [ADR-050](item:27268cd1-2dc2-519f-a69f-99bad621e0f1); the push gate's licence check recognises font files
- **MUST** keep fonts out of the size budget of the first load (PF5), with their own budget for the background download

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-061"   # no font requested before the app is usable; every font file has an approved licence
```

why: The system font keeps startup fast; project themes may bring their own font (UX decision [D-37](item:bf9e8fd4-9324-5773-b833-f1300742fb6b)), and nearly all good open fonts use the OFL.

Source: [ADR-061-shipped-fonts.md](item:acf46933-f26e-5b3d-b2ba-1d9510e0ba2a)

title: ADR-063 Terms: item, note, branch, node
note:
applies_to: `docs/**`, `src/**`, `tests/**`

- **MUST** use these terms in documents, code, tests and the test id catalogue:
  - **Item:** the thing in the tree: a title, a note, tags, and optionally a theme and views (later pictures and files); what it is (thought, idea, project, topic, vision) is the user's to decide, and an item can grow
  - **Thought:** the user-facing word for an item, used in the texts the user reads (UX decision [D-140](item:4fec508f-8d98-5cf1-9104-57384c68e905)); documents, code, tests and test ids say item, except when quoting a user-facing text or giving an example
  - **Note:** the optional longer text of an item (unchanged from today's glossary)
  - **Branch:** an item together with everything below it
  - **Node:** how an item appears in the tree, its line and place; a technical term for rendering and specifications
- The glossary of `architecture.md` uses these terms
- **MUST** use the renamed event types, fields and link scheme (done before the first release, while nothing is stored): `item.created`, `item.title-changed`, `item.note-changed`, `item.moved`, `item.deleted`, `item.restored`, `item.tagged`, `item.untagged`; fields `itemId`, `afterItemId`, `fromItemId`, `toItemId`; links `[text](item:<id>)`; test ids such as `item-title`

verify:

```bash
grep -rnE 'node\.(created|moved|deleted|restored|title-changed|note-changed|tagged|untagged)|\(node:' src tests docs/architecture.md | wc -l   # expect 0
```

why: Items grow from a single thought into projects or visions; a neutral term common to outliners leaves the meaning to the user (UX decision [D-45](item:ec0ed326-4a12-50f8-8564-6c575e213459)).

Source: [ADR-063-terms.md](item:b37c4ccc-f367-50df-9119-c3ba2f6da5e5)

title: ADR-064 UI work follows the UX concept
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Client*/**`, `tests/specify/**`

- **MUST** read the UX principles, the terms and the decisions of [ux-concept.md](https://github.com/AdventureDevelopment/ThoughtTree/blob/main/docs/ux-concept.md) that concern the screen before changing UI behaviour or look; where a decision and the code differ, the decision wins until the owner changes it
- **MUST** show an HTML sketch to the owner before building a new screen or a visibly new part of one, and build only the chosen variant; store the chosen sketch in `docs/ux/sketches/` and link it from its decision (UX decisions [D-46](item:e4313538-bd80-5421-a1cf-cb2fb80be671), [D-47](item:41d8579a-79f7-5bcd-b357-8549b5d5ba45))
- **MUST** use only the semantic design tokens for colour, font, spacing and density; **MUST NOT** use literal colours or sizes in components
- **MUST** name the UX decisions a UI specification secures (for example `D-12`) in the specification, as ADR ids are named in tests
- **MUST** attach to every pull request that changes UI: screenshots generated from the UI specifications (phone and tablet, light and dark), the link to the chosen sketch, and the link to the pull request's preview address (Azure Static Web Apps, [ADR-047](item:f453748f-2df8-508e-8da7-2db2f3dbda84))
- **MUST** fill the UI checklist of the pull request template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`, created together with the agent guide): principles checked, terms used, tokens only, sketch linked, screenshots attached, keyboard paths and screen reader names, roles and announcements (checked by specs and component rules) covered
- **MUST** point to this ADR and to the UX concept from the agents' entry file (`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`), so every agent starting UI work reads them

verify:

```bash
grep -rnE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b' --include=*.razor --include=*.css src/ThoughtTree.Client | grep -v tokens | wc -l   # expect 0: no literal colours outside the token files
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-064"   # every UI specification names at least one UX decision
```

why: UX intent reaches agents only through what they are pointed to; a binding rule, a pull request checklist and the entry file together act as the definition of done for UI work (UX decision [D-48](item:25c1bffe-c9f3-5374-b0f5-2b22801f7288)).

Source: [ADR-064-ui-follows-ux-concept.md](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d)

title: Code and test harness
note: Project boundaries, deterministic time and concurrency, the protected harness

title: ADR-027 Domain and Contracts projects
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

- **MUST** keep domain logic (events, projection, conflicts, clock, and the command logic that decides which events a user action writes) in ThoughtTree.Domain, used by the client side only (Client.App, Client, simulation, later native app)
- **MUST** share only ThoughtTree.Contracts (envelope, export format, API data) between client and server
- **MUST NOT** reference ThoughtTree.Domain from the server projects (ThoughtTree.Server, ThoughtTree.Server.Core)
- **MUST NOT** use browser, JavaScript interop, storage, network or async I/O in ThoughtTree.Domain; these APIs are listed in Domain's banned API file

verify:

```bash
dotnet build -warnaserror   # banned APIs in Domain are compile errors
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-027"   # architecture rules (ArchUnitNET)
```

why: The server cannot decrypt events; domain logic stays pure and testable.

Source: [ADR-027-project-dependencies.md](item:2c349d75-22e1-556d-8905-d4a3ea845146)

title: ADR-034 Replaceable time and randomness
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

- **MUST** obtain time only through `TimeProvider`
- **MUST** obtain ids, nonces and random values only through a replaceable generator
- **MUST NOT** call `DateTime.Now`, `DateTime.UtcNow`, `DateTimeOffset.Now`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, `Stopwatch`, `Environment.TickCount`, `Guid.NewGuid`, `new Random`, `Random.Shared` or `RandomNumberGenerator` outside the provider implementations
- **MUST** list these APIs in the banned API analyzer (`BannedSymbols.txt`), with the provider implementations as the only exemption

verify:

```bash
dotnet build -warnaserror   # banned APIs are compile errors
```

why: Every test must be exactly reproducible.

Source: [ADR-034-replaceable-time-random.md](item:5ce571c4-8e3f-5da8-8f84-cd3dade367d6)

title: ADR-035 Protected test harness
note:
applies_to: `tests/**`, `.github/**`

- **MUST NOT** change or delete stored test data in `tests/data/formats` or regression seeds in `tests/data/regression-seeds`; both are append-only
- **MUST NOT** change the reference model (`tests/secure/ThoughtTree.Domain.Model`) or the invariant catalogue without human approval
- **MUST NOT** accept new or changed snapshot files (`*.verified.*`) automatically, in CI or by an agent; changes need human approval
- **MUST NOT** change or delete specs in `tests/specify` without human approval
- **MUST** bring every change to `main` through a pull request; branch protection forbids direct pushes and requires the push gate
- **MUST** require the owner's review (CODEOWNERS) for changes to `tests/specify/**`, `tests/data/**`, the reference model, `*.verified.*`, `docs/**` and `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and for every change to the reviewer workflow and prompt (`.github/workflows/agent-review*`, `.github/agent-review/**`), the branch protection settings, anything holding secrets and the ADRs (`docs/adr/**`, human decision); an approval counts only for the latest push (new push, new approval)
- **MAY** let agents change `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the rest of `.github/**` (pull request template, other CI jobs) without the owner's review, if an independent reviewer agent approves the pull request as a required check; the reviewer runs from the workflow on `main`, never from the pull request, sees only the diff and the rules, and must reject any change that weakens a safeguard, contradicts an ADR or widens agent permissions; until it exists the owner reviews these files too
- **MUST NOT** delete gate tests or weaken assertions without human approval
- **MUST** tag every test that secures an ADR with its id (`[Trait("ADR", "ADR-0xx")]`)
- **MUST** run the whole gate suite without Azure accounts, secrets or network
- **MUST** make every test deterministic; report seed and minimal counterexample on failure
- **SHOULD** add tests freely

verify:

```bash
git diff --diff-filter=DM origin/main...HEAD -- tests/data/formats tests/data/regression-seeds | wc -l   # expect 0; runs on every pull request against its base
git diff origin/main...HEAD -- tests/secure/ThoughtTree.Domain.Model | wc -l   # expect 0 unless approved
git diff --diff-filter=ADM origin/main...HEAD -- '*.verified.*' | wc -l   # expect 0 unless approved
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-035"   # reports removed or renamed test methods and changed assertions in the pull request
```

why: The harness is the specification agents work towards; weakening it hides defects.

Source: [ADR-035-protected-harness.md](item:97da0e50-9466-5514-9447-714d2e42b66a)

title: ADR-039 No uncontrolled concurrency or timers
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

- **MUST NOT** use `Thread`, `Task.Run`, `Parallel`, `ThreadPool`, `System.Threading.Timer`, `System.Timers.Timer` or `Task.Delay` without a `TimeProvider` in client logic, Domain or the server core
- **MUST** do all waiting and timing through `TimeProvider` (`Task.Delay(TimeSpan, TimeProvider)`, `TimeProvider.CreateTimer`)
- **MUST** list the forbidden APIs in the banned API analyzer for Domain, Client.App and Server.Core; in the Client and Server projects, where hosting code shares the project, architecture tests enforce them per namespace
- **MAY** use them in the thin hosting layers (ASP.NET Core endpoints, browser interop) where the simulation does not run

verify:

```bash
dotnet build -warnaserror   # banned APIs are compile errors
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-039"   # architecture rules
```

why: The simulation decides the order of everything; uncontrolled concurrency makes runs unrepeatable.

Source: [ADR-039-controlled-concurrency.md](item:ce9f785f-861c-58b1-a873-6e888183ca73)

title: ADR-053 Functional core, hexagonal shell
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

- **MUST** keep Domain pure: commands plus state give events, events plus state give the new state; no ports, no I/O
- **MUST** put use cases and UI state into the application layer, which defines the ports it needs
- **MUST** implement ports only in adapters, each with a fake for tests
- **MUST** let dependencies point only inwards: UI → Application → Domain; adapters → Application; Domain depends on nothing (the UI references Application only)
- **MUST** let the UI bind only to view models of the application layer; **MUST NOT** reference Domain from the UI
- **MUST NOT** introduce per-use-case ceremony (interactor, input and output ports, request and response models, presenters) or entities with behaviour as the centre
- **MUST** structure the server the same way: Server.Core with ports, store adapters, ASP.NET Core as the outer shell

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-053"   # architecture tests (ArchUnitNET)
```

why: Every kind of code has exactly one place; the rule is mechanically checkable; the core is testable without anything around it.

Source: [ADR-053-functional-core-hexagonal-shell.md](item:2c9781f1-be13-5f8a-a9d4-3d036ca9307a)

title: ADR-054 Code organisation: boundaries, feature folders, test intents
note:
applies_to: `src/**`, `tests/**`

- **MUST** keep the current six source projects (Domain, Contracts, Client.App, Client, Server.Core, Server); a further project, for example for a later native app, needs a real boundary and an ADR change
- **MUST NOT** add a project without a real boundary (deployment, sharing, reuse); **MUST NOT** add "Shared" or "Common" projects
- **MUST** separate layers inside a project by namespace and check them with architecture tests (for example: UI does not use browser adapters directly, endpoints do not use stores directly)
- **MUST** organise folders by feature, with the same feature names in every project
- **MUST** place tests by intent under `tests/specify`, `tests/secure` or `tests/confirm` (shared helpers in `tests/support`, stored data in `tests/data`), name projects by kind (`Specs`, `Properties`, `Model`, `Compatibility`, `Simulation`, `Rules`, `Contract`, `Security`, `Budgets`, `EndToEnd`, `Smoke`) and set the `Intent` trait
- **MUST** write specs with LambdaTale in domain language; **MUST NOT** change or delete a spec without human approval

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-054"   # architecture tests check project references, namespaces and test placement
```

why: Real boundaries where they help (deployment, sharing, reuse, `internal`); everything else stays light and is still checked.

Source: [ADR-054-code-organisation.md](item:df3866b1-6463-5e5e-931c-edf0e582acc6)

title: ADR-075 xUnit v2 and LambdaTale 2.9.x for all test projects
note:
applies_to: `tests/**`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `**/*.csproj`

- **MUST** use xUnit v2 (`xunit` 2.9.x) in every test project, because `bbv.LambdaTale` 2.9.x depends on `xunit.core` 2.9.x
- **MUST** write specs with `bbv.LambdaTale` 2.9.x ([ADR-054](item:df3866b1-6463-5e5e-931c-edf0e582acc6))
- **MUST NOT** reference xUnit v3 packages (`xunit.v3*`, `xunit` 3.x) or add another specification or BDD library
- **MUST** keep these versions in `Directory.Packages.props` only; changing them is a human decision made through the bet card

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-075"
! grep -rEn 'xunit\.v3|Include="xunit" Version="3' --include='*.csproj' --include='Directory.Packages.props' .   # no match
```

why: Specs are the specification agents work towards; the spec library and its test framework must not drift or be swapped while LambdaTale has no xUnit v3 support.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that staying on xUnit v2 with LambdaTale 2.9.x is worth the dependency on a niche library until LambdaTale supports xUnit v3.

- **Outcome:** Every specification is written in one readable domain-language style, with one test framework, from the first line of code.
- **Assumption:** LambdaTale stays maintained and compatible enough with the .NET version in use; xUnit v2 keeps working and receives fixes while it is needed; moving to xUnit v3 later is a contained change in the test projects.
- **Signal:** The owner's own look at the LambdaTale releases on nuget.org when a review trigger below is considered; no data is collected.
- **Review when:** LambdaTale publishes a release that supports xUnit v3 · xUnit v2 stops receiving fixes, or a new .NET or Playwright version no longer works with it · the maintainers of LambdaTale archive the repository or stop answering issues · an agent or the owner needs a spec feature LambdaTale does not offer.

Source: [ADR-075-xunit-v2-lambdatale.md](item:43a28926-e5a3-53d3-a909-876064c319d6)

title: ADR-076 No code plugins; extend by data, readable files or a fork
note:
applies_to: `src/**`

Owner decision 2026-11-17 (Zettelkasten session), accepted by the owner 2026-11-19.

- **MUST NOT** load or run code that is not part of the app's own build: no plugin or extension mechanism, no loading of assemblies, scripts or WebAssembly modules at run time from user content, files, trees or addresses
- **MUST NOT** add an interface through which outside code reads decrypted content or uses the key handle
- **MAY** offer extension by data only, interpreted by the app's own code with fixed rules: templates ([ADR-068](item:10565c29-e7be-5e3f-bfaa-6249e2241cab)), views ([ADR-062](item:3ecc302d-7862-5524-8174-9dff17cce88a)), relation types, tags, themes shipped with the app ([ADR-060](item:bf684b01-1e00-5613-b339-982fb1ed2313)), and declarative import profiles
- **SHOULD** name the readable export and import ([ADR-019](item:ffcefe90-c6a9-5c6a-b05b-325df4472983)) as the way to work on a tree with other tools, outside the app, and back
- **MUST** leave custom code to forks: the code is Apache 2.0 ([ADR-049](item:323f7312-2d27-5929-8f16-1e5f607c12e4)) and a self-hosted package serves its own app with its own policy on its own origin ([ADR-045](item:4ed194a5-683a-5f25-9867-341f6922bd57)); the hosted app never widens its policy for it

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-076"   # architecture test: no run-time loading of assemblies or modules (for example Assembly.Load, AssemblyLoadContext, dynamic import) outside the app's own startup
```

why: Code inside the app sees decrypted content and the key handle; in a shared tree it reads the thoughts of people who never agreed to it, so a warning to the installer cannot make it safe; it would also break the strict CSP ([ADR-045](item:4ed194a5-683a-5f25-9867-341f6922bd57)), the bans on AI ([ADR-071](item:1bc7e63d-dcfc-5adb-87b2-dc10128daf48)) and third-party requests ([ADR-030](item:68a5428c-3b63-557c-b2c1-4957cf63343a)), and the tested formats.

Source: [ADR-076-no-code-plugins.md](item:b8a306fd-710e-56cb-9810-1852a57a0e04)

note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server.Core/**`, `src/ThoughtTree.Server/**`

- **MUST** keep the server logic (registration, device tokens, duplicate detection, event store) in ThoughtTree.Server.Core
- **MUST NOT** reference ASP.NET Core from ThoughtTree.Server.Core

title: ADR-046 Infrastructure as code, deployment without stored secrets
note:
applies_to: `infra/**`, `.github/**`

- **MUST** create test, production and the pull request previews only from Bicep templates in `infra/` (Azure Static Web Apps in release 1, Azure Container Apps once a sync server exists)
- **MUST** keep test and production identical apart from parameters
- **MUST** sign in from GitHub Actions to Azure through OpenID Connect federation; **MUST NOT** store deployment secrets

title: ADR-047 One container image everywhere
note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`, `infra/**`, `.github/**`

- **MUST** serve release 1, which has no sync server, as a static app from Azure Static Web Apps, with a preview address per pull request and the security headers of [ADR-045](item:4ed194a5-683a-5f25-9867-341f6922bd57) from its configuration file
- **MUST**, once a sync server exists, ship one image containing the server and the static client app, served from one origin
- **MUST** run the same image in test, production (Azure Container Apps) and self-hosting; differences only by configuration
- **MUST** select the store by configuration: the Azure store on Azure, SQLite on a volume for self-hosting
- **MUST NOT** run SQLite on Azure file shares
- **MUST** speak plain HTTP in the container and rely on a reverse proxy for HTTPS; **MUST** provide a Docker Compose example with a reverse proxy that obtains certificates automatically

verify:

```bash
dotnet test --filter "ADR=ADR-047"   # deployment smoke tests run against the image; when: server
```

why: What is tested is exactly what runs; one origin keeps the Content Security Policy simple.

**Bet card**

**TL;DR:** We bet that one image everywhere is worth the cold start after idle, because what is tested is exactly what runs. (Applies once a sync server exists; release 1 is served as a static app.)

- **Outcome:** One artifact for test, production and self-hosting; simple delivery; near-zero cost through scaling to zero.
- **Assumption:** The cold start after idle (a few seconds) is acceptable, because the app starts from the PWA cache and only sync waits; the free monthly allowance of Container Apps covers normal use.
- **Signal:** Feedback that sync is slow to start; Azure costs; server counters; the time from app start until the first sync completes (timing mark, visible in the diagnostics view and performance reports).
- **Review when:** Azure costs exceed the free allowance · repeated feedback says the first sync is too slow · Azure changes the free allowance or scale-to-zero behaviour of Container Apps.

Source: [ADR-047-one-container-image.md](item:f453748f-2df8-508e-8da7-2db2f3dbda84)

note:
applies_to: `src/ThoughtTree.Server*/**`, `.github/**`

- **MUST** scan the image for vulnerabilities in CI and rebuild when the base image gets security updates

Source: [ADR-048-image-supply-chain.md](item:f28ac9f0-7e3e-57e1-b894-d03695509d25)
