note: Questions from the open-decisions table that the owner decided without an ADR of their own; the decision is recorded in that table's row.

title: Size limits: import, font and server limits

note:
Still open after the stored numbers were decided ([ADR-087](item:0fbcadf7-3838-57a9-a1d6-07178194dfbb)):

- Before release 1: limits of a readable import (unpacked size, number of files), including a note longer than 50,000 characters in an imported vault; the budget for fonts downloaded in the background ([ADR-061](item:acf46933-f26e-5b3d-b2ba-1d9510e0ba2a)), not measured by the spike.
- Before the first server release: maximum request size; maximum events and storage per account.

title: Size limits: stored numbers
note: Decided by the owner 2026-11-25 (spike 1 decision 6), accepted as [ADR-087](item:0fbcadf7-3838-57a9-a1d6-07178194dfbb): padding buckets 512 B to 16 KiB, above that a multiple of 16 KiB, for event payloads only; note at most 50,000 and title at most 1,000 characters; user name at most 32 characters, server address at most 100 ASCII characters, one tree per pairing code; counted as code points after normalisation ([ADR-029](item:60a30705-4e16-547f-9365-4d928fe34dc1)); the UI enforces the limits and warns (sketch first, [ADR-064](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d)). Load budgets PF5, PF8, PF9 set 2026-11-25.

Owner, 2026-11-27, discussed; the lifecycle state and the terms are decided (see "Archive and erase: lifecycle state and terms"). Still open:

1. Archive details: children, the conflict with unseen changes (today `seen`, [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d)), archived items in search, links, relations, export, the map and tag counts; the restore view (sketch, [ADR-064](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d)).
2. Events and content separated (option B, Verraes's "forgettable payloads"; "crypto-shredding" weighed and not chosen): events hold structure and a `contentId`; title and note text in content blobs (id derived from the event id, own nonce and padding), possibly missing or erased; exchange asks which blobs each side has; no event id, signature or hash covers blob content. Waits for spike 2.
3. Real erasure, `item.content-erased`: deletes an item's blobs on every device that syncs and leaves an erased marker, kept for good; the UI states the limits.

Amends [ADR-005](item:84511883-937f-5636-b827-bee45d72fa11), [ADR-015](item:0a4a5821-6c8b-5175-936c-4ba123adbdc3), [ADR-016](item:ba97a8fe-3504-582c-b0ac-ecfe4bfd41f3), [ADR-018](item:145e6add-bf20-5378-a075-0ef31b6a908d), [ADR-063](item:b37c4ccc-f367-50df-9119-c3ba2f6da5e5), [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e), [ADR-078](item:77cb2789-955d-5774-ad8d-96da9c92986e), [ADR-082](item:f593841b-7318-58f3-8ca0-6f42beea0253), [ADR-087](item:0fbcadf7-3838-57a9-a1d6-07178194dfbb) and [D-26](item:2ed08a3b-769f-54ca-90f6-81429784abc0), [D-53](item:b6076109-fa9d-57fe-8352-007279b26153), [D-59](item:f6ef1160-560a-5ed2-a7d8-89cf5cadd058), [D-69](item:9114a2be-a731-5771-a10a-4610da1b9bbf), [D-99](item:28f1cdfb-e65a-59a8-9a6d-6d123f3b3238), [D-119](item:f5fc796f-a73c-5aee-924f-fda75da80668); check [ADR-085](item:30ed9a2b-2231-599a-8304-9a5a8d14fb7a) before renaming events.

**Settle:** after spike 2, before INV-13 (step 2a) and before release 1 fixes the stored formats; then one `Proposed` ADR.

title: Archive and erase: lifecycle state and terms
note:
Decided by the owner, 2026-11-27:

- An item's state is `Lifecycle { Live, Archived }`; there is no deleted state. Planned with it: `item.lifecycle-changed` replaces `item.deleted` and `item.restored`.
- Terms: "erase" (German "endgültig löschen…", asking first), after GDPR Art. 17, for the irreversible action; "archive" ("archivieren") for the everyday one; "delete" is used for neither.

No ADR yet; one `Proposed` ADR follows the open decision.

How a tree survives the loss of all devices: the details of the recovery code, the backup file and its flow, beyond the decided direction.

**Settle:** later.

title: Key backup: a random recovery code in its own backup file
note: Direction decided for release 1 scope (owner, 2026-11-16): a random recovery code rather than a passphrase (Web Crypto offers only PBKDF2, weak against guessing); the recovery-code-wrapped key lives in a separate backup file, not in the exchange file header ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)); the key stays random and is only wrapped for backup.

Still open:

- random blob ids, not content hashes
- padding or fixed-size chunks to hide file size
- server blob storage next to the event log (affects the store and the free tiers)
- fetching blobs only when needed
- files in exports
- when blobs of deleted items may be removed

**Settle:** later.

title: Binary data: separate encrypted blobs
note: Rule decided: pictures and files are separate encrypted blobs referenced from events ([ADR-022](item:4bb51fd5-b1a6-503d-9a52-d8f9caf33887)).

title: Linked Obsidian vault (later idea)

note:
A linked vault that re-imports and re-exports on request, with ThoughtTree's encrypted log staying the truth and file changes becoming ordinary events (conflicts visible as usual). Builds on the identity rules of the Obsidian import and export and needs folder access (store app or desktop Chromium).

**Settle:** later.

title: Obsidian vault bridge: not a live interface on a vault
note: Decided by the owner, 2026-11-17: ThoughtTree is not a live interface on an Obsidian vault. A PWA cannot open a folder on iPad; the vault would replace the event log as the truth ([ADR-002](item:92164dbe-21ee-55af-bc65-472f8ec4a151): no history, undo or visible conflicts); its files are plaintext at rest ([ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)); Obsidian, plugins and file sync would write outside the conflict model. Not in release 1.

Open for later: the sketch ([ADR-064](item:2b937f07-3185-55a9-9eb0-bc66af3e2a1d)) and a UX decision extending [D-97](item:f5e08082-2869-5d7f-a753-3230c1ab1e25): (1) where the scope is chosen, (2) how a hit shows its tree, (3) what opening a hit in another tree does and how the user goes back, (4) what shows while other indexes load, (5) the privacy sentence; whether several trees' keys must be unwrapped at once (each tree has its own index and key, [ADR-073](item:43633a32-ed5d-5734-b4af-16d4c581810e)); the phone budget. A first step could be a quiet line "Also in Zettelkasten · 4".

**Settle:** later.

title: All-trees search: out of release 1, search per tree
note: Moved out of release 1 by the owner on 2026-11-19 ([D-186](item:84e4b048-39d7-5334-9e06-e1772e906858)): search stays per tree (open tree or focused branch); searching all trees on the device is an idea for later. Earlier history: decided for release 1 on 2026-11-16.
